a40.speaker: Maneo Ntšike, 74-year-old resident of Qoaling
a40.name: Maneo Ntšike
a40.title: 74-year-old resident of Qoaling
a40.speech: "This was in 2016, and we were promised compensation once the project was completed. Some people were relocated, but those of us whose property was damaged have been fighting for compensation to no avail," ; "In trying to get help, we have been given the runarounds by MCC, the contractor, and WASCO, who shift blame as all of them refuse to take responsibility," ; "WASCO did not fix the leak. They just cut off my water supply and accused me of using the water. I was devastated," ; "I have come to terms with the loss of my furniture, but what worries me most is having to share a room with my grandson because the rest of the house is uninhabitable. I am always worried that the house could collapse, especially with the windy season approaching. Developments are meant to uplift us, but this one feels like a curse,"

a40.speaker: Matšepang Kolobe, affected resident of Qoaling
a40.name: Matšepang Kolobe
a40.title: affected resident of Qoaling
a40.speech: "I have tried patching up the walls and dealing with the water, but the leaks just keep coming. It has affected my business badly. While others charge M750 to M800 for two-roomed units, I still charge M600 just to get tenants. Before the road construction, we never had these issues," ; "We have been knocking on different doors since 2020. No one seems interested in solving this problem. We are open to relocation if necessary because we are just tired of living like this,"

a40.speaker: Makoae Tšiame, area chief, Qoaling
a40.name: Makoae Tšiame
a40.title: area chief, Qoaling
a40.speech: "We have tried everything in our power to get assistance, but nothing has been done. We have been told the contractor is responsible for compensation, but no one knows where he is,"

a40.speaker: 'Makatleho Mosala, Maseru City Council spokesperson
a40.name: 'Makatleho Mosala
a40.title: Maseru City Council spokesperson
a40.speech: Said the cases are being handled individually, not collectively. Explained that MCC documents properties with photographs before projects begin to assess damages afterward. Said she was on a field visit and therefore could not provide specific information until her return.

a40.speaker: Rethabile Lefantsatsa, WASCO spokesperson
a40.name: Rethabile Lefantsatsa
a40.title: WASCO spokesperson
a40.speech: Said this was the first time they had heard of the crisis, and promised to visit the affected community to gather information. "We were not aware of this case. However, WASCO has insurance to compensate those whose property has been damaged due to our operations. If the claims are valid, the residents are eligible for compensation,"

a68.speaker: Council of Ministers of the Federal Government of Somalia (Cabinet)
a68.name: Council of Ministers of the Federal Government of Somalia (Cabinet)
a68.speech: Stated that Sharmarke Farah, appointed Director-General of the National Bureau of Statistics, brings with him a wealth of experience having served as an economic researcher and in social sector development, including lead technical expert roles with the UN, World Bank, DfID, USAID, and the private sector.

a92.speaker: Nicki Minaj, American rapper
a92.name: Nicki Minaj
a92.title: American rapper
a92.speech: Shared that her vision for the song was to blend her signature hip-hop energy with the vibrant essence of Afrobeats, and believed Davido, with his catchy melodies and lyrical brilliance, was the perfect collaborator to bring that unique vibe to life. Praised Davido as an exceptional writer and melody maker, and expressed her delight in working with him, citing their mutual respect as a key factor in their creative synergy. Revealed that she invited Davido to join the project to enhance its Afrobeat tempo and feel, making the track stand out. Responded: "That man is an incredible writer & melody maker. It's always a pleasure working with him b/c of our mutual respect for one another. I asked him to be a part of it to bring out the Afro beats tempo/feeling in it a bit more. Nigeria to the world."

a92.speaker: Fan (anonymous social media user)
a92.name: Fan (anonymous social media user)
a92.speech: "What drew you to Davido for the song 'If It's Okay'? In my opinion, he was an ideal choice for this incredible masterpiece! He was speaking that ish," the user wrote.

a181.speaker: Dana Hyde, Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a181.name: Dana Hyde
a181.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a181.speech: "Access to reliable electricity is essential for communities and this element came up again in the discussions I had with actors on the ground" ; "The second MCA compact will modernise the energy distribution network and improve the production framework, because it is important for us that the infrastructure be able to properly absorb the energy it carries" ; "We want to ensure the sustainability of the investments of the American people in Benin as well as those of the private sector."

a181.speaker: Dana Hyde, CEO of MCC
a181.name: Dana Hyde
a181.title: CEO of MCC
a181.speech: For her, the choice to focus this compact's investments exclusively on the energy sector goes without saying and is in line with the "Power Africa" initiative launched by American president Barack Obama.

a181.speaker: Dana Hyde, CEO of MCC
a181.name: Dana Hyde
a181.title: CEO of MCC
a181.speech: Gives assurances that the programme will support the process of clearing the State's debts towards the Beninese electrical energy company (SBEE) and above all those of SBEE towards the Electrical Community of Benin (CEB); and welcomes the passage of the law on public-private partnership in Benin.

a243.speaker: Dr. Amir Aman, Ethiopian Minister of Health
a243.name: Dr. Amir Aman
a243.title: Ethiopian Minister of Health
a243.speech: "Digitizing the system alone doesn't mean getting solutions end to end rather it is working on the mind set of all stakeholders." ; "Digitalizing health systems mean a lot for the Ministry as it corrects the data and improves information about the health of our population."

a243.speaker: Sean Jones, USAID Mission Director
a243.name: Sean Jones
a243.title: USAID Mission Director
a243.speech: "In addition to simply expanding digital health systems and strengthening the skills of today's medical professionals, we are also increasing our focus on developing the leaders of tomorrow to drive health innovations far into the future."

a243.speaker: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia
a243.name: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia
a243.speech: According to the Ministry of Health, currently 88 percent of health centers are digitized and the rest 22 percent will be incorporated in this fiscal year, adding that the support from USAID is pertinent to the move.

a678.speaker: FARM-STEW (faith-based organization in South Sudan)
a678.name: FARM-STEW (faith-based organization in South Sudan)
a678.speech: Has expressed profound gratitude to USAID South Sudan for a vital donation of essential equipment.

a678.speaker: Lasu Charles, FARM-STEW Executive Director
a678.name: Lasu Charles
a678.title: FARM-STEW Executive Director
a678.speech: "Today is a day to give thanks to God and to celebrate what we have received." ; "We have been given items from the RASS project, which was funded by USAID. Sometimes, when things seem to go wrong, they can turn out to be blessings. After USAID closed, they realized they had many assets still available. They also remembered FARM-STEW and didn't forget about it." ; "Among the items received is the Land Cruiser parked outside, along with several printers, computers, scanners, and monitor screens. We also received 2 to 3 cameras, motorcycles, and other equipment."

a678.speaker: Doreen Okech Arkangelo, FARM-STEW Training Coordinator
a678.name: Doreen Okech Arkangelo
a678.title: FARM-STEW Training Coordinator
a678.speech: Attributed the organization's humble beginnings and success to their unwavering dedication and diligent work: "We have witnessed the hand of God." ; "Initially, we received USD 50,000 for one year because our work was simple, everyone was doing well, and the community was very happy. Once that USD 50,000 was used up, they provided us with another $50,000, instructing us to use it for six months." ; "Soon after, a larger amount of $400,000 was granted to us, to be used over two years... That was the beginning of our growth. You see, when you are faithful with small things, using them diligently, God will multiply your efforts."

a678.speaker: Wani Wilson, board member of FARM-STEW
a678.name: Wani Wilson
a678.title: board member of FARM-STEW
a678.speech: Regarded the gifts as a testament to the trust bestowed upon the organization: "As board members, we see this as a trust bestowed upon us by the organization, recognizing the potential they have observed in us." ; "We are truly grateful, especially knowing that they work with many other partners, yet their decision to support FARM-STEW reflects their confidence and commitment in us." ; "As board members, we are dedicated to ensuring that the equipment provided to us is used effectively to expand FARM-STEW's programs. Additionally, we are committed to maintaining accountability for all the assets entrusted to us."

a774.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in Namibia
a774.name: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in Namibia
a774.speech: Says levels of viral load in nine out of 10 children with the virus are below detection levels.

a774.speaker: Vann Rolfson, Acting Country Representative of USAID
a774.name: Vann Rolfson
a774.title: Acting Country Representative of USAID
a774.speech: Noted that having nine out of 10 HIV-infected children below the detection level or virally suppressed is another step for Namibia to reach the UN 95-95-95 goals.

a786.speaker: European Union (communique of 15 October)
a786.name: European Union (communique of 15 October)
a786.speech: Announced that it had provided 98 million CFA francs of humanitarian aid to the victims of the floods in Mali, in addition to another 656 million CFA francs of humanitarian aid already allocated to the country: "this funding will help the Malian Red Cross respond to the immediate needs of households affected by the floods, particularly in terms of food, shelter, hygiene and logistical support" ; the intervention also includes "the establishment of training programmes to prepare these communities to better withstand future disasters through risk reduction and climate adaptation measures" ; "this funding falls within the framework of the EU's overall contribution to the Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF) of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC)."

a786.speaker: European Union (communique of 15 October)
a786.name: European Union (communique of 15 October)
a786.speech: Stated that the floods caused significant damage to infrastructure, loss of human life and large-scale population displacement: "With a total of 649 reported flood incidents, 259,795 people have been affected, the most affected being the Segou region, with 73,080 people impacted" ; "sanitation facilities, such as toilets and wells, have also suffered significant damage: 12,325 toilets/latrines have been affected and 4,360 wells have been flooded, exacerbating problems linked to hygiene and access to drinking water."

a786.speaker: European Union / European officials
a786.name: European Union / European officials
a786.speech: Said Mali has always faced floods, particularly during the rainy season from June to November, but that "the frequency and intensity of these floods have increased over the years, caused in part by the climate crisis and deforestation, with dramatic consequences for rainfall patterns and soil stability."

a888.speaker: Tanzania Communications Regulatory Authority (TCRA)
a888.name: Tanzania Communications Regulatory Authority (TCRA)
a888.speech: Has announced that mobile phone service providers in the country have maintained strong quality levels while expanding coverage and penetration.

a888.speaker: Dr Jabiri Bakari, TCRA Director General
a888.name: Dr Jabiri Bakari
a888.title: TCRA Director General
a888.speech: Revealed that the June 2025 communications sector status report shows all five Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) performing within the Quality of Service (QoS) parameters, with only minor variations; said TCRA monitored MNO services across 14 regions between April and June 2025, assessing compliance in 17 key areas, with average performance standing at 92.8 per cent; said the evaluation covered efficiencies in call handover between communication towers and voice quality for users on the move, and that data transfer speeds to mobile devices were also measured.

a888.speaker: Dr Jabiri Bakari, TCRA Director General
a888.name: Dr Jabiri Bakari
a888.title: TCRA Director General
a888.speech: “Reliable and high-quality mobile communication services are vital for Tanzania’s economic growth, as they facilitate business operations, improve access to information and drive digital innovation.”

a888.speaker: June 2025 communications sector status report
a888.name: June 2025 communications sector status report
a888.speech: Highlights Kilimanjaro region as the leader in average mobile data download speeds among the 17 regions inspected, with an average download speed of 22.47 megabits per second, surpassing the industry average of 19.4 Mbps.

a1232.speaker: Tabia Ussene, resident of the village of Mecufi
a1232.name: Tabia Ussene
a1232.title: resident of the village of Mecufi
a1232.speech: said “I sleep right here. The children stay in this shack we built and the adults spend the nights out here. There are six children who sleep in this bed. The house, the (other) beds and all our things disappeared.”

a1232.speaker: Eusébio Rachide, Cyclone Chido victim in Mecufi
a1232.name: Eusébio Rachide
a1232.title: Cyclone Chido victim in Mecufi
a1232.speech: lamented “Neither tarpaulin, nor food, nor any help have we had, at least so far. The list of those affected by the cyclone was drawn up a long time ago so that they would receive aid, but so far nothing. We have only seen vehicles passing by with things for other communities. Almost everyone has already received something, but here, in the main village of Mecufi, so far no aid at all.” ; added “We here in Mecufi are only watching the aid pass by and be distributed in other communities. We are asking the Government for help, because we can no longer bear the suffering.”

a1232.speaker: District administrator of Mecufi
a1232.name: District administrator of Mecufi
a1232.speech: was absent and unreachable by telephone when the newspaper visited Mecufi (no comment obtained).

a1232.speaker: National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD)
a1232.name: National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD)
a1232.speech: was not available to explain the lack of humanitarian aid in the village of Mecufi (no comment obtained).

a1316.speaker: Save the Children (statement)
a1316.name: Save the Children (statement)
a1316.speech: Said at least four African countries will run out of specialised life-saving food for severely malnourished children in the next three months due to shortages caused by aid cuts ; said supplies were getting dangerously low in Nigeria, Kenya, Somalia and South Sudan of high-energy biscuits, peanut-based Plumpy'Nut paste and other treatments known as Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF) ; said some clinics in the four African countries were turning to less-effective treatments for malnourished children ; said stocks in Kenya are expected to run out in October and that RUTF supplies in Nigeria, Somalia and South Sudan would run out within three months ; said that globally, funding cuts are expected to cut off nutrition treatment this year to 15.6 million people across 18 countries, including 2.3 million severely malnourished children.

a1316.speaker: Yvonne Arunga, Save the Children's regional director for East and Southern Africa
a1316.name: Yvonne Arunga
a1316.title: Save the Children's regional director for East and Southern Africa
a1316.speech: "At a time when global hunger is sky-rocketing, the funding that could save children's lives has been cut because of recent aid cuts."

a1316.speaker: Save the Children
a1316.name: Save the Children
a1316.speech: Did not name specific donors or funding reductions in its statement.

a1316.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1316.name: Donald Trump
a1316.title: US President
a1316.speech: Has said cuts to humanitarian aid are needed to ensure that grants align with his "America First" agenda and that other countries shoulder more of the burden.

a1316.speaker: Government officials from the four countries (Nigeria, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan)
a1316.name: Government officials from the four countries (Nigeria
a1316.title: Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan)
a1316.speech: Did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

a1316.speaker: Reuters (report)
a1316.name: Reuters (report)
a1316.speech: Reported in May that cuts by the Trump administration left 60,000 to 66,000 metric tons of food, including 1,100 tons of fortified biscuits, stranded in warehouses for months earlier this year.

a1316.speaker: US government
a1316.name: US government
a1316.speech: Later agreed to hand over 600 tons of the biscuits to the U.N. World Food Programme but said it would have to destroy nearly 500 tons which expired last month.

a1316.speaker: US State Department
a1316.name: US State Department
a1316.speech: Announced it would provide $93 million for RUTF supplies to treat more than 800,000 children suffering from severe acute malnutrition in 13 countries, including Nigeria, Sudan, Kenya and Democratic Republic of Congo.

a1324.speaker: South Sudan National Bureau of Standards (SSNBS) (statement)
a1324.name: South Sudan National Bureau of Standards (SSNBS) (statement)
a1324.speech: Said in a statement that the consignment underwent destination inspection and conformity assessment, including laboratory testing based on East African Standards (EAS) ; said the consignment was officially classified as non-compliant and unfit for human consumption ; is urging all importers and traders to strictly comply with both national and regional standards and to fully cooperate in ongoing quality control efforts ; previously raised alarm over the safety standard of some Ugandan imports, impounding tonnes of goods over the presence of dangerous chemicals.

a1324.speaker: Ashgan Paulina Edward, Acting Director General for Technical Operation at SSNBS
a1324.name: Ashgan Paulina Edward
a1324.title: Acting Director General for Technical Operation at SSNBS
a1324.speech: Said the results confirmed that the grains were physically damaged, contained high levels of impurities and foreign materials, and showed signs of spoilage ; said the grain shipment was a donation from a foreign country to one of the churches in South Sudan's Western Equatoria State ; "We had a dumping of yellow peas and maize grain in Nimule border post. It has taken long and when it reached to Nimule, the inspection revealed that the product is not fit for human consumption." ; "Even when we took it to the lab to count the insects, because it has a lot of insects in it, and when we counted, we found that even like the heart of the seed is not having any value. The product is not supposed to enter to the country because no one is supposed to eat it." ; "Even if it is a donation, but we are so concerned even about the safety of each and every one in this country. The quantity is 19 bags, and then the 19 bags, one bag is 200 kg in weight and in one truck. So, 19 big bags."

a1324.speaker: SSNBS official social media page (photos)
a1324.name: SSNBS official social media page (photos)
a1324.speech: Photos shared on the SSNBS' official social media page showed the truck carrying what appears to be a spoiled maize grain.

a1324.speaker: Uganda and South Sudan bureaus of standards (joint resolution)
a1324.name: Uganda and South Sudan bureaus of standards (joint resolution)
a1324.speech: On January 14, 2024, resolved to jointly clamp down on cross-border trade in counterfeit goods by ensuring better standard and quality of their respective exports.

a1531.speaker: Vitumbiko Mumba, Malawi's Minister of Trade and Industry and running mate to President Lazarus Chakwera
a1531.name: Vitumbiko Mumba
a1531.title: Malawi's Minister of Trade and Industry and running mate to President Lazarus Chakwera
a1531.speech: Announced that Botswana is ready to start importing Malawi's Kilombero rice, and revealed at a campaign rally in Chintheche, Nkhata Bay, that a high-level delegation from his ministry will travel to Botswana at the end of the month to finalize trade talks that will open the rice export market for Malawians: "Let me break the news today: When Botswana's President, Duma Boko, recently visited Malawi, he tasted our Kilombero rice. Just two days later, I received a call from Botswana's Minister of Trade saying their President was impressed and wants Malawi's rice to be sold in Botswana" ; "The market is there now. All we need is to grow more rice and take advantage of this opportunity."

a1531.speaker: Vitumbiko Mumba, Malawi's Minister of Trade and Industry
a1531.name: Vitumbiko Mumba
a1531.title: Malawi's Minister of Trade and Industry
a1531.speech: Emphasized that the deal is a direct result of the government's diplomatic and trade efforts, and added that the development would create more jobs and boost rural incomes: "This is not just about trade—it's about creating employment for our people. With more demand, more hands will be needed in the fields, in processing, and in transportation."

a1531.speaker: Botswana's Minister of Trade (reported by Mumba)
a1531.name: Botswana's Minister of Trade (reported by Mumba)
a1531.speech: Called Mumba to say their President was impressed by Malawi's Kilombero rice and wants it to be sold in Botswana.

a1646.speaker: David Stevenson, WFP's Country Director in Nigeria
a1646.name: David Stevenson
a1646.title: WFP's Country Director in Nigeria
a1646.speech: "The African Development Bank's support is timely and comes as a lifeline for those struggling to feed themselves amidst rising food prices and economic turmoil" ; said communities which, after years of conflict and violence, started rebuilding their lives were struck by the floods and once again displaced, meaning more and more people cannot support themselves and their families.

a1646.speaker: Cadre Harmonisé food security analysis (November 2024, 26 states and the federal capital)
a1646.name: Cadre Harmonisé food security analysis (November 2024
a1646.title: 26 states and the federal capital)
a1646.speech: projects that 33 million people in Nigeria will face food insecurity by August 2025.

a1646.speaker: Abdul Kamara, African Development Bank Director General in Nigeria
a1646.name: Abdul Kamara
a1646.title: African Development Bank Director General in Nigeria
a1646.speech: "I hope that this additional funding will mitigate the suffering of vulnerable people on the brink of acute hunger at a time when more Nigerians than ever need humanitarian assistance." ; "I commend the Federal Government of Nigeria and WFP for the continuous efforts to operate in such a challenging environment to improve the lives of Nigerian families."

a1655.speaker: Manuel Gonçalves, Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Mozambique
a1655.name: Manuel Gonçalves
a1655.title: Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Mozambique
a1655.speech: praised the work carried out by UNICEF in defending and protecting the rights of children in Mozambique and meeting their basic needs ; praised the support provided by UNICEF in humanitarian assistance and special care for children affected by terrorism in Cabo Delgado ; expressed the desire to see the existing cooperation between Mozambique and UNICEF in favour of the well-being of Mozambican children strengthened.

a1655.speaker: Statement received by the newsroom
a1655.name: Statement received by the newsroom
a1655.speech: indicates that the vice-minister also expressed the desire to see the existing cooperation between Mozambique and UNICEF in favour of the well-being of Mozambican children strengthened.

a1655.speaker: Mary Louise Eagleton, new UNICEF Representative to Mozambique (post on X)
a1655.name: Mary Louise Eagleton
a1655.title: new UNICEF Representative to Mozambique (post on X)
a1655.speech: "Great pleasure to present my credentials to H.E. Manuel José Gonçalves, Mozambique's Dept. Minister of Foreign Affairs & Cooperation. Looking forward to close partnership as we continue work to protect & promote children's rights in Mozambique. Estamos juntos para cada criança!"

a1799.speaker: Jonathan Richter, USAID resident representative in Benin
a1799.name: Jonathan Richter
a1799.title: USAID resident representative in Benin
a1799.speech: Said that fake antimalarials represent 25% of all counterfeit medicines, which are the cause of a large number of deaths that occur when people unknowingly and in good faith use fake or substandard medicines to prevent or treat malaria.

a1799.speaker: Jonathan Richter, USAID resident representative in Benin
a1799.name: Jonathan Richter
a1799.title: USAID resident representative in Benin
a1799.speech: "It is in the interest of the Government of the United States to do this for security reasons and more specifically in USAID's interest because of its long-term investments in Benin's health system with a particular focus on the fight against malaria." ; went on to specify that the fight against counterfeit medicines is a collective battle, because, he said, one of the greatest challenges in this fight is the multisectoral nature of the response required, and to that end it is important to establish alliances among several institutions.

a1799.speaker: Parfait Adjakidjè, Director General of the National Laboratory for Quality Control of Medicines and Medical Consumables (Lncq)
a1799.name: Parfait Adjakidjè
a1799.title: Director General of the National Laboratory for Quality Control of Medicines and Medical Consumables (Lncq)
a1799.speech: Indicated that high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) is particularly useful for separating high molecular weight materials that have very low volatility and cannot be separated by gas chromatography, and that the main areas of application are biotechnology, the life sciences and the pharmaceutical industry.

a1799.speaker: Jacob Bonou, head of microbiology and physico-chemistry at the Lncq
a1799.name: Jacob Bonou
a1799.title: head of microbiology and physico-chemistry at the Lncq
a1799.speech: Added, explaining that this system serves to identify solutes, molecules and pharmaceutical products; it is also used to quantify molecules; sometimes it makes it possible to determine impurities in these products; it is therefore a complete device that makes it possible to carry out quality control of pharmaceutical products.

a1799.speaker: Lucien Toko, Chief of Staff of the Ministry of Health of Benin
a1799.name: Lucien Toko
a1799.title: Chief of Staff of the Ministry of Health of Benin
a1799.speech: Expressed his full satisfaction with this gem, which will make it possible to secure the health of the population. "We are going to arm ourselves further so that the products that enter the country are stopped at the laboratory level," he hammered home.

a1799.speaker: Market studies (2014-2015)
a1799.name: Market studies (2014-2015)
a1799.speech: Revealed that nearly half of all private outlets in several large markets in Benin sell fake antimalarials.

a1975.speaker: Hodan Osman, president of the Somali Development and Reconstruction Bank
a1975.name: Hodan Osman
a1975.title: president of the Somali Development and Reconstruction Bank
a1975.speech: Said the closure of the U.S. Agency for International Development earlier this year hit Somalia's economy and tax revenues: "In Somalia (it) really impacted our GDP" ; said the country faced a broader economic hit: "It also had (a) severe impact just on the economy alone that we weren't really thinking about."

a2060.speaker: U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement on its official website)
a2060.name: U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement on its official website)
a2060.speech: Announced that, effective Friday, February 7, USAID will place all direct-hire personnel worldwide on administrative leave, and that for USAID staff stationed outside the United States the agency, in collaboration with local missions, is formulating a plan to arrange and fund return travel to the U.S. within 30 days.

a2060.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Namibia (no response)
a2060.name: U.S. Embassy in Namibia (no response)
a2060.speech: nbc News reached out to the U.S. Embassy to establish how many local jobs the closure of USAID will affect and how this closure will directly impact the work being done by the programme; the nbc will give an update once the embassy has responded.

a2097.speaker: Dinesh Balsingh, Airtel Nigeria CEO
a2097.name: Dinesh Balsingh
a2097.title: Airtel Nigeria CEO
a2097.speech: Has reaffirmed the telecom giant's commitment to delivering superior connectivity and fostering digital inclusion ; noted that the proposed tariff adjustments aim to ensure the long-term sustainability of the sector while unlocking significant benefits for Nigerian consumers ; in an op-ed he explained that "For over a decade, tariffs have remained static despite the dramatic increase in operating expenses, which have surged by over 300% in the last 18 to 24 months alone. To continue providing high-quality services and meeting the growing demand for digital connectivity, it has become essential to realign our pricing structure with economic realities."

a2097.speaker: Dinesh Balsingh, Airtel Nigeria CEO
a2097.name: Dinesh Balsingh
a2097.title: Airtel Nigeria CEO
a2097.speech: Highlighted the substantial investments required to maintain and expand telecommunications infrastructure: "The increasing demand for digital services across sectors such as education, banking, and healthcare requires us to continually upgrade our networks to deliver more capacity and improve service quality. These investments come at a cost, one that must be shared proportionally to guarantee long-term viability," he observed.

a2097.speaker: Dinesh Balsingh, Airtel Nigeria CEO
a2097.name: Dinesh Balsingh
a2097.title: Airtel Nigeria CEO
a2097.speech: Added: "By enabling us to expand coverage, strengthen network security, and introduce cutting-edge technologies, the adjustments will directly enhance the quality of connectivity for Nigerians. Our priority is to ensure that no one is left behind in the country's digital transformation journey."

a2097.speaker: Dinesh Balsingh, Airtel Nigeria CEO
a2097.name: Dinesh Balsingh
a2097.title: Airtel Nigeria CEO
a2097.speech: Emphasised that these adjustments will be implemented with affordability in mind, ensuring minimal impact on consumers: "Our commitment to quality service remains unwavering. While significant tariff adjustments have become necessary, we understand the importance of gradual implementation to support our customers' financial positions."

a2104.speaker: International Institute for Sustainable Development (analysis on rethinking tax incentives in the mining sector in Africa)
a2104.name: International Institute for Sustainable Development (analysis on rethinking tax incentives in the mining sector in Africa)
a2104.speech: Has urged African governments, including Malawi, to rethink mining tax incentives which it says are a significant source of potential revenue loss for African governments; observed that long seen as a mandatory tool to attract foreign investments, mining tax incentives have lost their allure; argues that while mineral resources represent a significant opportunity for domestic resource mobilisation, most African countries have failed to fully realise the expected revenues from the sector due to several external and internal factors, including poorly designed and overly generous tax incentives ; "African governments might achieve greater benefits by focusing on improving socio-economic infrastructure, providing comprehensive geological data, and fostering political and economic stability rather than relying solely on tax incentives. For a long time, the advice given to countries was to provide economic stimuli to compete for investment and to boost the economy. That narrative has since changed. Currently, there is a developing global consensus on the need to limit tax competition."

a2104.speaker: International Institute for Sustainable Development
a2104.name: International Institute for Sustainable Development
a2104.speech: According to the institute, after decades of intense tax competition between countries, the international community, through the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting, is finally addressing the race to the bottom by introducing a global minimum tax of 15 percent.

a2104.speaker: Grain Malunga, minerals and geology expert (paper titled 'Proposed Investment Incentives for the Mining Sector')
a2104.name: Grain Malunga
a2104.title: minerals and geology expert (paper titled 'Proposed Investment Incentives for the Mining Sector')
a2104.speech: Said generalised assumptions for the use of tax incentive programmes must be carefully analysed through mine specific considerations outside agriculture, manufacturing and tourism incentive lens; commodity price risk can bring financial loss for producers and consumers: "Global geopolitics has the ability to polarise nations leading to a decline in demand for new investments and marketability of mineral products."

a2104.speaker: Simplex Chithyola-Banda, Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a2104.name: Simplex Chithyola-Banda
a2104.title: Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a2104.speech: Acknowledged the extraction sector's exposure to exploitation which could undermine the sector's economic benefits.

a2161.speaker: United Nations
a2161.name: United Nations
a2161.speech: Warned, at a press conference on Monday, that the Gaza Strip is going through its most serious humanitarian crisis since the beginning of the latest round of the conflict between Israel and Hamas in October 2023, stating that the situation has reached its worst point since the start of hostilities 18 months ago.

a2161.speaker: Stephane Dujarric, Spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General
a2161.name: Stephane Dujarric
a2161.title: Spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General
a2161.speech: "The Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs warns that the humanitarian situation will probably be the worst of the last 18 months since the start of hostilities. It has now been a month and a half since any supplies were allowed to cross the borders into Gaza, by far the longest interruption of this kind to date. Humanitarian aid must be above any kind of political decision. And I believe there were Security Council resolutions, and I think we have been very clear about the fact that humanitarian aid must be freely accessible to all who need it."

a2161.speaker: Stephane Dujarric, Spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General
a2161.name: Stephane Dujarric
a2161.title: Spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General
a2161.speech: Went further in holding Israel to account: "Israel has responsibilities, under international law, as an occupying power, to adequately provide basic services and humanitarian aid to the population of Gaza. This is not happening. We will point out the situations, the violations, in our view, of international law."

a2161.speaker: UN officials
a2161.name: UN officials
a2161.speech: According to UN officials, Israel's attacks in Gaza have intensified in recent days, resulting in a large number of civilian casualties and further damage to the already fragile infrastructure of the Gaza Strip.

a2164.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, President of Namibia
a2164.name: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah
a2164.title: President of Namibia
a2164.speech: Has urged all Namibians to reject divisive tendencies such as tribalism, regionalism, and discrimination in order to build a unified and inclusive society.

a2164.speaker: Kaweche Kaunda, son of Zambia's founding President Kenneth Kaunda
a2164.name: Kaweche Kaunda
a2164.title: son of Zambia's founding President Kenneth Kaunda
a2164.speech: As Namibia celebrates its 36th Independence celebrations, has cautioned Namibians not to fall into the trap of division.

a2164.speaker: Alick Banda, Archbishop of the Cosmopolitan Archdiocese of Lusaka, Zambia
a2164.name: Alick Banda
a2164.title: Archbishop of the Cosmopolitan Archdiocese of Lusaka, Zambia
a2164.speech: Appeared before the Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC) for questioning but opted to remain silent.

a2164.speaker: Mulilo Kabesha, Attorney General of Zambia
a2164.name: Mulilo Kabesha
a2164.title: Attorney General of Zambia
a2164.speech: Has demanded access to the late Edgar Lungu's body for identification and authentication purposes; through the lawyers representing the state in South Africa, has warned that failure to grant access will prompt them to seek an order from the Pretoria High Court.

a2164.speaker: Nellie Mutti, Speaker of the National Assembly of Zambia
a2164.name: Nellie Mutti
a2164.title: Speaker of the National Assembly of Zambia
a2164.speech: Has ordered that the daughter of the late former Zambian President Edgar Lungu, Tasila Lungu, an elected Member of Parliament, should appear before her office 14 days after the burial of her father; failure to do so would see her lose her seat.

a2164.speaker: Mutale Nalumango, Vice President of Zambia
a2164.name: Mutale Nalumango
a2164.title: Vice President of Zambia
a2164.speech: In the Zambian Parliament's debate on the late Edgar Lungu's funeral impasse, called on the family to take charge.

a2225.speaker: African leaders
a2225.name: African leaders
a2225.speech: Have been quick to congratulate Donald Trump on his re-election and are calling for cooperation with mutual respect.

a2225.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a2225.name: Donald Trump
a2225.title: US President-elect
a2225.speech: Reportedly referred to African nations, among others, as "shithole" countries at a private January 2018 meeting.

a2225.speaker: Raila Odinga, veteran Kenyan politician
a2225.name: Raila Odinga
a2225.title: veteran Kenyan politician
a2225.speech: Has shrugged off Trump's comments, telling AFP: "This is now – another, new Trump."

a2225.speaker: Ronak Gopaldas, analyst at the Institute for Strategic Studies, Africa
a2225.name: Ronak Gopaldas
a2225.title: analyst at the Institute for Strategic Studies, Africa
a2225.speech: Wrote before the election: "Under a Trump administration, with its 'America First' mantra, trade policy would likely be insular and transactional" ; "Given Trump's scepticism of multilateral frameworks, AGOA's continuation could be legitimately under threat" ; "Although Africa might not feature prominently on his agenda, Trump's first administration did push for trade deals with select African countries, suggesting a preference for bilateral engagement."

a2225.speaker: General Michael Langley, US Africa Command chief
a2225.name: General Michael Langley
a2225.title: US Africa Command chief
a2225.speech: Said in September the US military was discussing with other African partners what comes next after the Sahel withdrawal to "reset and recalibrate" assets.

a2225.speaker: US State Department
a2225.name: US State Department
a2225.speech: According to the US State Department, the US is the largest single donor to Africa, with figures at nearly US$4 billion for the sub-Saharan continent in 2024.

a2225.speaker: South African newspapers
a2225.name: South African newspapers
a2225.speech: Are already discussing whether PEPFAR, the US programme to help combat HIV and AIDS, will continue under Trump.

a2225.speaker: US officials
a2225.name: US officials
a2225.speech: Say the PEPFAR programme has saved 25 million lives in two decades.

a2225.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a2225.name: Donald Trump
a2225.title: US President-elect
a2225.speech: Has already promised broad tariffs on foreign imports, has criticised the billions of dollars in US spending for Ukraine, dismisses climate change as a scam and has pledged to reverse Biden's climate-friendly measures.

a2225.speaker: Mohamed Adow, Kenyan activist and director of Power Shift Africa
a2225.name: Mohamed Adow
a2225.title: Kenyan activist and director of Power Shift Africa
a2225.speech: Wrote in a statement responding to Trump's election: "Climate action is urgent. Victims of climate catastrophes in the Global South need life-saving support. The world has dealt with a Trump presidency that included the withdrawal of the US from the Paris Agreement. His return could see a second exit from the agreement by America, and the cancellation of its climate commitments. This is a moment of profound apprehension in global climate diplomacy."

a2241.speaker: Dr Dalitso Kabambe, UTM President (party statement responding to the State of the Nation Address)
a2241.name: Dr Dalitso Kabambe
a2241.title: UTM President (party statement responding to the State of the Nation Address)
a2241.speech: Said President Dr Lazarus Chakwera's State of the Nation Address attempted "to paint a picture of progress and resilience" but that "the reality on the ground which is experienced by each and every Malawians starkly contrasts with the President's narrative" ; "President Dr Chakwera has proven himself a master of excuses, a craftsman of obfuscation, and a leader tragically disconnected from the daily struggles of the Malawian people." ; "this speech was nothing more than a desperate attempt to mask incompetence, mismanagement, and a trail of broken promises with empty rhetoric." ; "For over 1,684 days, President Dr Chakwera and his government have failed to lead. Instead of making life better for Malawians, they have excelled in making excuses - blaming COVID-19, the war in Ukraine, past administrations, and even labeling critics as enemies."

a2241.speaker: Dr Dalitso Kabambe, UTM President (party statement)
a2241.name: Dr Dalitso Kabambe
a2241.title: UTM President (party statement)
a2241.speech: "Mr. President, the time has come for you to honor your own promise - step down, as you vowed to do if you failed to fix this country in your first two years. You have failed. Malawians will no longer tolerate failure disguised as governance."

a2241.speaker: Dr Dalitso Kabambe, UTM President (party statement)
a2241.name: Dr Dalitso Kabambe
a2241.title: UTM President (party statement)
a2241.speech: Said the 25% and 44% devaluations of the Kwacha "were an economic disaster that plunged inflation beyond 30%, making basic commodities and services unaffordable", and listed price increases since 2020 for maize (MWK 7,500 to MWK 85,000 per 50kg bag), fuel (MWK 690 to MWK 2,300 a litre), fertilizer (MWK 18,000 to over MWK 90,000), tomatoes, sugar, electricity tariffs, data, medicine and school fees ; said the economy has barely scraped 2% annual growth against 2.7% population growth, poverty stands at 75%, inflation has risen from 7% to 33%, interest rates have doubled from 13% to 26%, the kwacha has moved from K732/US$ to K1,700/US$ officially and over K4,200/US$ on the parallel market, import cover has contracted from 3 months to less than 2 weeks, and public debt has soared from K4 trillion to over K15 trillion "with nothing to show for" ; said his reckless economic policies, forcing companies to sell off their forex reserves at lower rates, have forced businesses to shut down while others flee to neighbouring countries, leaving thousands jobless.

a2241.speaker: Dr Dalitso Kabambe, UTM President (party statement)
a2241.name: Dr Dalitso Kabambe
a2241.title: UTM President (party statement)
a2241.speech: Said that while Chakwera claims to have empowered the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB), "corruption has flourished under his watch", citing months without an ACB Director and scandals such as Butcher Gate, Pharmacy Gate, and "the infamous Bridgin Foundation scam", and said "Dr Chakwera has protected corrupt individuals in his government while punishing whistleblowers and political opponent."

a2241.speaker: Dr Dalitso Kabambe, UTM President (party statement)
a2241.name: Dr Dalitso Kabambe
a2241.title: UTM President (party statement)
a2241.speech: Said that over 5 million Malawians are starving and that the government "has politicized aid, taking away the dignity of vulnerable Malawians", making people stand in long queues for a bag of maize ; said many of the projects Chakwera boasted about "were possibly funded but simply never happened" and were mere "cosmetic band-aids on a hemorrhaging nation", while commending China AID for the M1 Rehabilitation and other international partners for projects that have been fulfilled.

a2241.speaker: Dr Dalitso Kabambe, UTM President (party statement)
a2241.name: Dr Dalitso Kabambe
a2241.title: UTM President (party statement)
a2241.speech: Said the President and the MCP "are disingenuous, fake, and downright liars" for invoking the name of the late Dr Saulos Klaus Chilima (SKC) while having "persecuted him relentlessly", and pledged to deliver the "Blueprint for Real Transformational Change" SKC left.

a2241.speaker: Dr Dalitso Kabambe, UTM President (party statement)
a2241.name: Dr Dalitso Kabambe
a2241.title: UTM President (party statement)
a2241.speech: Pledged that once sworn in as President in September, UTM would cut inflation to single digits within a year, stabilise the Kwacha and ensure abundance of forex, cut lending rates to around 10% and reduce taxes; implement Mega Farms in every district within the first year; create district-level industries; produce 10 to 15 million metric tonnes of maize in 5 years; invest about K500 billion annually of public and private funds into mining, manufacturing and tourism and root out corruption including ensuring independence and proper funding of the ACB; introduce Universal Healthcare Insurance; deliver decentralisation with a minimum of K100 billion annually per district; create smart cities and smart villages and District Development Agencies; and establish a Ministry of Social Housing capacitating the Malawi Housing Corporation with 1 Trillion Kwacha over 5 years to build no less than 1 million new homes ; "COME SEPTEMBER, LETS VOTE BASED ON PERFORMANCE! YOU ARE THE EMPLOYER - FIRE THOSE WHO HAVE FAILED YOU!"

a2241.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi (State of the Nation Address)
a2241.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a2241.title: President of Malawi (State of the Nation Address)
a2241.speech: Delivered what he called a report on "progress", boasting about "systemic surgery", claiming to have empowered the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB), speaking of food security, and boasting about increasing salaries.

a2241.speaker: MCP Press Secretary (voice note)
a2241.name: MCP Press Secretary (voice note)
a2241.speech: Was "caught admitting the truth in a widely circulated voice note: they misreported their achievements, and to them, lying to Malawians is acceptable because it's an election year", stating that the details don't matter, that misreporting is justified because they are dealing with an "enemy", and referring to Malawians demanding accountability as "the enemy".

a2241.speaker: Reports from districts including Mzimba, Chikwawa, Mangochi, Chitipa, Rumphi, Phalombe, Ntchisi, Kasungu and Likoma
a2241.name: Reports from districts including Mzimba
a2241.title: Chikwawa, Mangochi, Chitipa, Rumphi, Phalombe, Ntchisi, Kasungu and Likoma
a2241.speech: Confirm "what Malawians have long suspected - many of these projects were possibly funded but simply never happened."

a2241.speaker: Social media commentary (cited in the statement)
a2241.name: Social media commentary (cited in the statement)
a2241.speech: Summed up the record as: "1st SONA in 2021 - 'I am doing Surgery'; 2nd SONA in 2022 - 'I am doing Surgery'; 3rd SONA in 2023 - 'I am doing Surgery'; 4th SONA in 2024 - 'I am doing Surgery'; 5th SONA in 2025 - 'I am doing Surgery'. Pardon Doctor, is the patient still alive?"

a2368.speaker: 2025 Global Aids Update (UNAIDS report)
a2368.name: 2025 Global Aids Update (UNAIDS report)
a2368.speech: According to the report, the United States' decision to make cuts to the US President's Emergency Plan for Aids Relief (PEPFAR) could result in six million extra HIV infections and four million more Aids-related deaths by 2029.

a2368.speaker: UNAIDS report
a2368.name: UNAIDS report
a2368.speech: "HIV programmes in low- and middle-income countries have been rocked by sudden, major financial disruptions that threaten to reverse years of progress in the response to HIV" ; "Wars and conflict, widening economic inequalities, geopolitical shifts and climate change shocks - the likes of which are unprecedented in the global HIV response - are stoking instability and straining multilateral cooperation" ; "The sudden withdrawal of the single biggest contributor to the global HIV response disrupted treatment and prevention programmes around the world."

a2368.speaker: UNAIDS report
a2368.name: UNAIDS report
a2368.speech: According to the report, people acquiring HIV and those dying from Aids-related causes were at their lowest levels in "more than 30 years"; however, by the end of 2024, the decline in numbers was "not sufficient" to end Aids as a public threat by 2030; in new infections, there was a 56 percent decline in sub-Saharan Africa, which is home to half of all people who "acquired HIV globally in 2024"; "Five countries, mostly from sub-Saharan Africa, were on track to achieve a 90 percent decline in new infections by 2030 compared with 2010."

a2368.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAIDS Executive Director
a2368.name: Winnie Byanyima
a2368.title: UNAIDS Executive Director
a2368.speech: Told the Reuters news agency that "prevention was hit harder than treatment" by the cuts. "Key populations were the worst affected ... they depended on tailored services by community leaders, and those were the first to go."

a2368.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAIDS Executive Director
a2368.name: Winnie Byanyima
a2368.title: UNAIDS Executive Director
a2368.speech: On European donors scaling back development assistance: "They've told us that it has to do with defence spending," she said, adding that figures showed "global health [spending] peaked and then it also started declining with the Ukraine war."

a2607.speaker: Stanley Similo, nbc Director General
a2607.name: Stanley Similo
a2607.title: nbc Director General
a2607.speech: “Some of us look great because we are standing on the shoulders of giants” — said during an interview focused on the broadcaster’s extensive coverage of the Founding President’s final farewell.

a2607.speaker: Lazarus Jacobs, nbc Board Chairman
a2607.name: Lazarus Jacobs
a2607.title: nbc Board Chairman
a2607.speech: Says it is important for the corporation to own Miss Namibia as a subsidiary where every Namibian can take ownership; he says Miss Namibia is not just a pageant, but an Ambassador.

a2607.speaker: Lazarus Jacobs, nbc Board Chairperson
a2607.name: Lazarus Jacobs
a2607.title: nbc Board Chairperson
a2607.speech: Says the corporation has been at the forefront of supporting young people in furthering their career in broadcasting, despite opposite views by some.

a2607.speaker: Stanley Similo, nbc Director General
a2607.name: Stanley Similo
a2607.title: nbc Director General
a2607.speech: Expressed pride in the project of premiering 14 short films in partnership with ‘No Plot Productions’ while calling on the business community to support the local film industry.

a2607.speaker: Lazarus Jacobs, Namibian Broadcasting Corporation Chairperson
a2607.name: Lazarus Jacobs
a2607.title: Namibian Broadcasting Corporation Chairperson
a2607.speech: Urged the public to vote for Miss Namibia Cassia Sharpley to be among the semi-finalists of the Miss Universe pageant.

a2607.speaker: Lazarus Jacobs, NBC Board Chairperson
a2607.name: Lazarus Jacobs
a2607.title: NBC Board Chairperson
a2607.speech: Has expressed dismay over the release of a financial audit report involving the Namibian Broadcasting Corporation, which a local newspaper made available to the public this week while the document had not previously been shared with the national broadcaster.

a2623.speaker: Republic of Djibouti (communiqué)
a2623.name: Republic of Djibouti (communiqué)
a2623.speech: Condemns in the strongest terms the heinous crime perpetrated by the Israeli occupation forces through the bombing of the Baptist hospital in the Gaza Strip, which constitutes a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law; warns against the collapse of the health system in the Gaza Strip as a result of the continuing Israeli atrocities, and calls on the international community to assume its responsibilities in order to put an end to these atrocities and to protect innocent civilians.

a2623.speaker: Republic of Djibouti (communiqué)
a2623.name: Republic of Djibouti (communiqué)
a2623.speech: Condemns in the strongest terms the attacks carried out against the Zamzam and Abu Shouk camps for displaced persons in Darfur, Sudan, which caused the death and injury of dozens of people, in flagrant violation of international humanitarian law; reiterates the imperative of guaranteeing the protection of civilian populations and of humanitarian actors, underlines the importance of safe, rapid and sustained access to humanitarian aid, expresses its full support for all regional and international efforts to restore peace, security and stability in Sudan, and extends condolences to the bereaved families.

a2644.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (meeting of Wednesday 11 September)
a2644.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (meeting of Wednesday 11 September)
a2644.speech: Decided to commission a study mission for the definitive repair of the sand-retention groyne at the port of Cotonou.

a2644.speaker: Independent international expert (report)
a2644.name: Independent international expert (report)
a2644.speech: It emerges from the expert's report that the primary cause of the infrastructure's defectiveness is negligence in its design.

a2644.speaker: African Development Bank, Project Summary Note (June 2023)
a2644.name: African Development Bank
a2644.title: Project Summary Note (June 2023)
a2644.speech: According to the Project Summary Note published by the African Development Bank, the total financing of these projects amounts to 461.6 million euros, or 302.8 billion CFA francs, to be financed by various lenders as well as by the equity of the Autonomous Port of Cotonou.

a2644.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (meeting of 11 November 2020)
a2644.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (meeting of 11 November 2020)
a2644.speech: Gave its agreement for contracting with the architectural firm Koffi & Diabate for the project management mission for the Maritime Affairs Centre.

a2683.speaker: Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation of Somalia
a2683.name: Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation of Somalia
a2683.speech: Announced a decisive move to protect consumers and bolster local industry by appointing a special committee to investigate the importation of low-quality food and vegetables, and ordered the task force to prepare a comprehensive report, within a brief timeframe, on the markets and supply chains responsible for bringing these goods into the country.

a2820.speaker: Voice of America (Voz da América)
a2820.name: Voice of America (Voz da América)
a2820.speech: Reports that Manuel Chang, addressing the judge before the sentence was read out, said he was “ashamed” of his actions and deeply regretted the harm caused.

a2820.speaker: Manuel Chang, former Mozambican Finance Minister
a2820.name: Manuel Chang
a2820.title: former Mozambican Finance Minister
a2820.speech: Said he was “ashamed” of his actions and that he deeply regretted the harm caused ; also begged the judge to show “compassion” and to take into account in his sentence the almost six years he has already served in prison, of which four and a half years, according to him, in deplorable conditions in South Africa.

a2820.speaker: Nicholas Garaufis, US federal judge
a2820.name: Nicholas Garaufis
a2820.title: US federal judge
a2820.speech: In reading out the sentence, said he had taken into account the six years Chang has spent in prison and that within two and a half years he will be released and deported to Mozambique ; “The victims trusted Mr. Chang to manage their investments and the development of their country in a manner free of corruption,” Garaufis said at Chang's sentencing in the federal court in Brooklyn.

a2820.speaker: Prosecutors (US)
a2820.name: Prosecutors (US)
a2820.speech: Accused Manuel Chang of taking bribes from the shipbuilding company Privinvest in exchange for his approval of a Mozambican Government guarantee for loans from banks, including Credit Suisse, to three state-backed companies.

a2820.speaker: Manuel Chang's defence lawyers
a2820.name: Manuel Chang's defence lawyers
a2820.speech: Say they intend to appeal the sentence.

a3095.speaker: East African Community (EAC) and Southern African Development Community (SADC) (heads of state, extraordinary summit decision)
a3095.name: East African Community (EAC) and Southern African Development Community (SADC) (heads of state
a3095.title: extraordinary summit decision)
a3095.speech: Announced this Monday the designation of former Kenyan president Uhuru Kenyatta, former Nigerian head of state Olusegun Obasanjo and former Ethiopian prime minister Hailemariam Desalegn as peace facilitators to lead the regional peace efforts of the merged Luanda and Nairobi processes, giving them the mission of overseeing the implementation of the ceasefire between the parties to the conflict, coordinating humanitarian aid and supporting discussions between stakeholders with a view to a durable resolution in eastern DRC.

a3251.speaker: MacDonald Gondwe, Mzuzu City Council spokesperson
a3251.name: MacDonald Gondwe
a3251.title: Mzuzu City Council spokesperson
a3251.speech: Said the facility was closed on Saturday and would be reopened on May 31 after the maintenance ; Said they would focus on improving the pitch as it was bumpy and dusty during the dry season and muddy during winter: "Through our Department of Leisure, Parks and Environment, we have already started the work and we are optimistic that renovations would be completed by May 31, when the facility is expected to be reopened. We need to level the playing ground by applying soil and water." ; Said they were committed to rejuvenating the status of the stadium within the stated period ; "We apologise to stakeholders for the inconvenience."

a3251.speaker: Benjamin Thole, Mzuzu City Hammers General Secretary
a3251.name: Benjamin Thole
a3251.title: Mzuzu City Hammers General Secretary
a3251.speech: Said it was sweet and bitter news: "As a club we will now be spending over K700,000 on logistics to travel to Rumphi for each game. At the same time, it is a good development because the condition of the pitch is worrisome and it was affecting our performance."

a3251.speaker: Richard Chimwendo Banda, Minister of Local Government, Malawi
a3251.name: Richard Chimwendo Banda
a3251.title: Minister of Local Government, Malawi
a3251.speech: Said President Lazarus Chakwera had demanded for the construction of a new stadium in Mzuzu.

a3340.speaker: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
a3340.name: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni
a3340.title: Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
a3340.speech: Delivered a message in which she encouraged all actors to continue their efforts with rigour and humanity, respecting the principles of transparency, accountability and above all the dignity of the country's people. ; Stressed that, since 19 August 2003, hundreds of other humanitarian workers around the world have been victims of violence, injured or killed while working tirelessly to assist vulnerable populations in contexts of war, forced displacement, epidemics or climate disasters.

a3340.speaker: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
a3340.name: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni
a3340.title: Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
a3340.speech: Noted that this edition is being held in a global context still marked by complex security crises, forced displacement of populations, and increasingly frequent climate shocks; said that in regions such as the central Sahel, and particularly in the countries of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), lawless armed terrorist groups attack civilians gratuitously every day, disrupting community life and compromising their access to security, education, health and livelihoods. ; "Persistent insecurity, particularly in certain border areas, continues to cause displacement of refugees and internally displaced persons and makes access to basic services difficult for many families."

a3340.speaker: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
a3340.name: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni
a3340.title: Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
a3340.speech: Rejoiced that, by the grace of God and unlike previous years at the same period, the 2025 floods have so far not reached the alarming toll recorded last year, the result of unprecedented prevention efforts made possible by key measures: reconstruction and rehabilitation of waterways in cities such as Niamey and Maradi; intensive awareness campaigns via radio, television and community relays; early mobilisation of local actors and technical services; and active collaboration of populations living in flood-prone areas.

a3642.speaker: Xi Jinping, President of China
a3642.name: Xi Jinping
a3642.title: President of China
a3642.speech: Has said China will offer 200 million RMB, which is nearly D2 billion, to support The Gambia's development efforts, made as he met President Barrow on the sidelines of the FOCAC summit in Beijing.

a3642.speaker: Xi Jinping, President of China
a3642.name: Xi Jinping
a3642.title: President of China
a3642.speech: Commended The Gambia's support of China's global initiatives and reunification agenda.

a3642.speaker: State House of The Gambia (statement)
a3642.name: State House of The Gambia (statement)
a3642.speech: “During a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the FOCAC Summit, President Adama Barrow expressed gratitude for China's commitment to supporting his government's development agenda. The Gambian leader also reaffirmed The Gambia's support for China's Global Initiative and One China policy.”

a3642.speaker: Adama Barrow, President of The Gambia
a3642.name: Adama Barrow
a3642.title: President of The Gambia
a3642.speech: Expressed gratitude for China's commitment to supporting his government's development agenda; reaffirmed The Gambia's support for China's Global Initiative and One China policy; called for support in the digital economy and rural connectivity, emphasising that the partnership presents a golden opportunity to address global challenges such as peace and prosperity for a shared future; commended President Xi for the grants that made it possible to build roads and bridges in the Upper River and the Sir Dawda Kairaba Jawara International Conference Centre, and appreciated President Xi's gesture of sending a Special Envoy to attend the OIC Banjul Summit.

a3795.speaker: Musa al-Kony, deputy head of the Libyan Presidential Council
a3795.name: Musa al-Kony
a3795.title: deputy head of the Libyan Presidential Council
a3795.speech: Described the situation to the Italian Nova agency after his return from an international tour, on the sidelines of his visit to Washington ; called it a "traumatic experience" forcing Libyan officials to avoid flying over their own national territory due to the "presence of foreign mercenaries" and undermining Libya's sovereignty ; "This situation must end."

a3795.speaker: Nova agency (Italian)
a3795.name: Nova agency (Italian)
a3795.speech: Reports: "The plane was forced to change its return route from a trip abroad, as Russian troops stationed at a military base in the south of the country refused to grant permission to fly over their airspace."

a3795.speaker: Musa al-Kony, deputy head of the Libyan Presidential Council
a3795.name: Musa al-Kony
a3795.title: deputy head of the Libyan Presidential Council
a3795.speech: Noted that the independence of Fezzan, where, according to him, "Russian troops" are located, is very important for Italy, because there are "several very important infrastructure projects" in which Italy could participate "for its own benefit, as well as for Libya" ; concluded: "This initiative with a direct line across Libya to Africa will create a strong link with the Mediterranean and Italian interests on the continent."

a4021.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a4021.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a4021.title: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a4021.speech: Underlined the fundamental role of continental financial institutions, indispensable to Africa’s economic integration and sustainable development, and stressed the urgency of accelerating their creation and strengthening; in his view their effective establishment is an obligatory step to ensure the continent’s economic sovereignty: “It is imperative to accelerate the implementation of the African financial institutions, which are the fundamental pillars of this integration.” ; “There are constraints to be lifted for the implementation of this process, which must ultimately lead to the well-being of our populations and to Africa’s geopolitical affirmation on the international stage.”

a4021.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a4021.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a4021.title: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a4021.speech: Indicated that Africa still suffers from a low rate of industrialisation, limited access to energy and a worrying digital divide ; insisted on the need for African countries to take their destiny into their own hands by strengthening endogenous financing mechanisms: “The continent’s economic future rests on our capacity to develop solid institutions, able to respond to the needs of our populations and to foster inclusive and sustainable growth.”

a4021.speaker: Atlas of Africa 2024 (report)
a4021.name: Atlas of Africa 2024 (report)
a4021.speech: According to it, roughly 600 million people are still not connected to the electricity grid, thereby compromising the development of digital infrastructure and the emergence of an integrated and competitive economy.

a4021.speaker: African Union
a4021.name: African Union
a4021.speech: Advocates a coordinated approach among its member states, the Regional Economic Communities (RECs) and financial partners to overcome these obstacles; a coordination meeting has been instituted to follow the evolution of integration initiatives and propose suitable solutions.

a4026.speaker: National Drought Management Authority (NDMA) of Kenya (report)
a4026.name: National Drought Management Authority (NDMA) of Kenya (report)
a4026.speech: Said Monday that at least a million people in Kenya are struggling with food insecurity and in need of humanitarian assistance ; noted in a report released in Nairobi that the affected people are in 23 out of the country’s 47 counties, which are classified as arid and semi-arid ; revealed that households sold their harvests to cover other costs, often at the expense of maintaining healthy eating and chronic challenges associated with stunting.

a4026.speaker: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) (July report)
a4026.name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) (July report)
a4026.speech: Noted in a report in July that the number of food-insecure people in the Horn of Africa stands at 66.7 million, among them 39.1 million from six of eight IGAD member states, namely Djibouti, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda.

a4094.speaker: Yitbarek Semeane (PhD), director of inputs at the Agricultural Transformation Agency
a4094.name: Yitbarek Semeane (PhD)
a4094.title: director of inputs at the Agricultural Transformation Agency
a4094.speech: According to him, the project aims at improving smallholder farmers’ productivity, food security and incomes through the development of private sector driven and market-oriented agricultural supply and services ; “Agricultural productivity in Ethiopia is low, due largely to limited availability of inputs.”

a4094.speaker: Yitbarek Semeane (PhD), director of inputs at the Agricultural Transformation Agency
a4094.name: Yitbarek Semeane (PhD)
a4094.title: director of inputs at the Agricultural Transformation Agency
a4094.speech: Said farmers currently use agrochemicals they buy at informal markets, which are neither regulated nor checked, and that some of the chemicals are defective and entered the country through contraband.

a4094.speaker: Yitbarek Semeane (PhD), director of inputs at the Agricultural Transformation Agency
a4094.name: Yitbarek Semeane (PhD)
a4094.title: director of inputs at the Agricultural Transformation Agency
a4094.speech: Said the scale of agricultural activities in the regions and how the benefits of such shops could be maximised were the two primary criteria in selecting the four regional states ; “We want the shops to be run by professionals. The Agency will pay the first year salary of the staff, and the shop owner will continue from there.”

a4094.speaker: Studies (on agricultural input utilisation)
a4094.name: Studies (on agricultural input utilisation)
a4094.speech: Studies show that Ethiopia is one of the lowest countries in terms of agricultural input utilisation.

a4094.speaker: Alemitu Hordofa, owner and general manager of Bako Farm Service Centre, Oromia Regional State
a4094.name: Alemitu Hordofa
a4094.title: owner and general manager of Bako Farm Service Centre, Oromia Regional State
a4094.speech: Says the programme has been beneficial to both her and farmers of the area; when she opened the shop in mid-2017 she had eight employees, now the number has grown to 15, and she has managed to build two more satellite shops.

a4094.speaker: Alemitu Hordofa, owner and general manager of Bako Farm Service Centre, Oromia Regional State
a4094.name: Alemitu Hordofa
a4094.title: owner and general manager of Bako Farm Service Centre, Oromia Regional State
a4094.speech: Says that she is facing challenges in getting enough supplies due to the shortage of foreign currency to import the supplies.

a4094.speaker: Mohammed Aman, assistant professor of agri-economics and agri-business at Haramaya University
a4094.name: Mohammed Aman
a4094.title: assistant professor of agri-economics and agri-business at Haramaya University
a4094.speech: Argues that the shops should not be viewed as a single entity by the Agency, stating that input demand of the farmers will differ from region to region depending on ecology ; “The supply of the shops should be demand-driven.”

a4094.speaker: Mohammed Aman, assistant professor of agri-economics and agri-business at Haramaya University
a4094.name: Mohammed Aman
a4094.title: assistant professor of agri-economics and agri-business at Haramaya University
a4094.speech: Warns that the Agency should not roll out and keep being involved in both securing the supplies as well as ensuring input prices at the shops, arguing that the purchasing power of the farmers should determine the market price ; “We can’t expect a free market when there are few suppliers. Prices will go up.”

a4141.speaker: Dmitry Sytyi, director of the Russian House in Bangui
a4141.name: Dmitry Sytyi
a4141.title: director of the Russian House in Bangui
a4141.speech: Stressed that these actions are part of a broader approach. “We have already provided humanitarian aid to more than twenty African countries,” he said. According to him, these initiatives, though little publicized, attest to Russia’s growing commitment to humanitarian cooperation on the continent ; “Western media often remain silent about these actions, but for us, the essential thing is to respond to the needs of local populations,” he added.

a4141.speaker: Dmitry Sytyi, director of the Russian House in Bangui
a4141.name: Dmitry Sytyi
a4141.title: director of the Russian House in Bangui
a4141.speech: Explained, on the institution’s cultural and educational role: “Our mission is not limited to culture. We want to contribute to the human and social development of the CAR.”

a4141.speaker: President of the Central African Republic
a4141.name: President of the Central African Republic
a4141.speech: Hailed this initiative, calling Russian support “a source of hope for hundreds of families.” He also expressed his government’s desire to strengthen cooperation with Russia, particularly in the areas of health and social development.

a4170.speaker: Department of Disaster Management Affairs (DoDMA)
a4170.name: Department of Disaster Management Affairs (DoDMA)
a4170.speech: Has revealed that while the country needs K209.4 billion (about US$119 million) to roll out the national hunger plan, only K61.2 billion has so far been secured from the government and development partners, leaving K148.2 billion still unfunded.

a4170.speaker: Officials (unnamed)
a4170.name: Officials (unnamed)
a4170.speech: Fear that without urgent donor injections, food assistance could collapse halfway through the lean season.

a4170.speaker: Wilson Moleni, Commissioner for Disaster Management Affairs
a4170.name: Wilson Moleni
a4170.title: Commissioner for Disaster Management Affairs
a4170.speech: Said the situation is dire but insisted that the response will still target every affected person, even in districts not officially declared disaster zones ; “The total number of affected people is 4.2 million, and all of them will be assisted, whether they are in declared disaster districts or not.”

a4170.speaker: Wilson Moleni, Commissioner for Disaster Management Affairs
a4170.name: Wilson Moleni
a4170.title: Commissioner for Disaster Management Affairs
a4170.speech: Said funding so far has come from the Government of Malawi, the World Bank, UK Government, USAID, Irish Aid, Germany, Norway, the Netherlands, Korea, China, and the World Food Programme (WFP) — but the resources fall far short of the enormous need.

a4170.speaker: Malawi Vulnerability Assessment Committee (MVAC)
a4170.name: Malawi Vulnerability Assessment Committee (MVAC)
a4170.speech: Recently warned that prolonged dry spells and erratic rainfall have devastated crop yields, leaving millions without enough food until the next harvest.

a4170.speaker: Leonard Chimwaza, agriculture policy expert
a4170.name: Leonard Chimwaza
a4170.title: agriculture policy expert
a4170.speech: Described the situation as “a painful déjà vu” for a country that has spent decades battling cyclical hunger ; “It’s heartbreaking that year after year, Malawi finds itself in the same position—begging for billions to feed its people. The K148 billion gap is not just a number; it’s the difference between life and death for millions of poor Malawians.”

a4306.speaker: Liberia Electricity Regulatory Commission (LERC)
a4306.name: Liberia Electricity Regulatory Commission (LERC)
a4306.speech: Announces that the Liberia Electricity Corporation (LEC) has submitted a complete application for new electricity tariffs for the Commission’s approval, covering the period August 1, 2025, to July 31, 2028; notes that the management of LEC proposes a new customer category “Government” in its submission, in addition to its four previous customer categories.

a4306.speaker: Liberia Electricity Regulatory Commission (LERC)
a4306.name: Liberia Electricity Regulatory Commission (LERC)
a4306.speech: Informs the public that the tariffs currently being paid by customers shall remain the same until it announces a decision on the tariff proposal submitted by the LEC; says it shall organize a series of public hearings, stakeholder engagements, and outreach initiatives to ensure transparency and public participation in the review of the tariff proposal.

a4306.speaker: 2015 Electricity Law of Liberia, Section 8.1(2)
a4306.name: 2015 Electricity Law of Liberia
a4306.title: Section 8.1(2)
a4306.speech: Provides that “a licensee may not charge a customer any other tariff other than that determined or approved by the Regulator.”

a4306.speaker: Liberia Electricity Corporation (LEC) / Interim Management Team
a4306.name: Liberia Electricity Corporation (LEC) / Interim Management Team
a4306.speech: Had informed the Commission that the previous submission coincided with an internal transition, and the IMT was unfamiliar with the tariff application previously submitted by the former administration (in December 2024 the Commission granted the IMT’s request to withdraw the Corporation’s initial tariff application).

a4306.speaker: Claude J. Katta, Chairman of the Board of Commissioners (LERC)
a4306.name: Claude J. Katta
a4306.title: Chairman of the Board of Commissioners (LERC)
a4306.speech: “The Commission is committed to ensuring transparency and regulatory best practices throughout the tariff-setting process.”

a4401.speaker: Michael Usi, Vice-President of Malawi
a4401.name: Michael Usi
a4401.title: Vice-President of Malawi
a4401.speech: Called for changes to the international financial architecture to ensure that development aspirations of poor countries such as Malawi are delivered equitably: "We need enhanced voices of developing countries in decision-making spaces of international financial institutions including multi-lateral development banks. Debt relief, highly concessional loans, blended finance and official development assistance are essential for countries like Malawi facing disproportionate impact of global political and economic dynamics as well as climate and pandemic shocks." ; said Malawi will embrace innovative and transformative financial mechanisms such as digital and blended financing: "We urge enhanced support for trade infrastructure and market access, alongside fair multilateral trade rules so that we build effective public-private financial and capital markets" ; said Malawi has the appropriate legal and policy frameworks for digital financing but requires capacity enhancement in science, technology and innovation: "We must bridge technological gaps to empower youth and women for sustainable development" ; as a panellist at the Commission on the Future of Development Finance, reiterated the need for financing human capital expertise in the private and public sector, and acknowledged that all countries are operating in difficult environments but financing partners must not forget the positive outcomes of supporting programmes which have spill-over effects on human capital development.

a4401.speaker: Pedro Sanchez, Prime Minister of Spain
