a4401.name: Pedro Sanchez
a4401.title: Prime Minister of Spain
a4401.speech: Highlighted the urgency of collective action saying the platform represents "a critical opportunity to restore trust in multilateralism and deliver tangible financing".

a4401.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a4401.name: Antonio Guterres
a4401.title: UN Secretary-General
a4401.speech: Underscored the importance of the Seville Platform for Action as a catalyst for joint action and delivery.

a4543.speaker: Finances News Hebdo (Moroccan newspaper)
a4543.name: Finances News Hebdo (Moroccan newspaper)
a4543.speech: Reports that the Kingdom continues to record record performances in the tourism sector: by the end of February 2025 nearly 2.7 million tourists had crossed border posts, up 24% on last year, with 1.4 million visitors in February alone, up 22% year-on-year, driven in particular by the French and Spanish markets.

a4543.speaker: Lesiteinfo (Moroccan outlet)
a4543.name: Lesiteinfo (Moroccan outlet)
a4543.speech: Specifies that the National Water and Forests Agency (ANEF) and EUCAFOREST, a subsidiary of the CDG group, have signed an agreement to strengthen research and development in forest plantations, under the “Forests of Morocco 2020-2030” strategy, aiming to modernise silvicultural practices with an emphasis on technological innovation, varietal selection and adaptation to climate change.

a4543.speaker: TSA Algerie (Algerian outlet)
a4543.name: TSA Algerie (Algerian outlet)
a4543.speech: Reports a surge in the price of bananas, reaching 650 dinars per kilo against less than 400 previously.

a4543.speaker: Traders (Algerian merchants)
a4543.name: Traders (Algerian merchants)
a4543.speech: Said the price increase was due to speculative practices involving wholesalers and cold-storage managers.

a4543.speaker: El Watan (Algerian newspaper)
a4543.name: El Watan (Algerian newspaper)
a4543.speech: Announces that the Algerian government plans a reform of the mining code; the new text, to be submitted soon to Parliament, aims to remove certain restrictions, including the 51/49% rule, and to allow private investors to operate directly under a mining permit.

a4543.speaker: TunisieNumerique (Tunisian outlet)
a4543.name: TunisieNumerique (Tunisian outlet)
a4543.speech: Reports that the Ennahda Movement has demanded the release of its secretary general Ajmi Lourimi, arrested between 6 and 10 March without legal grounds according to the party.

a4543.speaker: Ennahda Movement (Tunisian party)
a4543.name: Ennahda Movement (Tunisian party)
a4543.speech: Demanded the release of its secretary general Ajmi Lourimi, arrested between 6 and 10 March without legal grounds according to the party; the arbitrary detention was denounced by lawyers and by the political formation.

a4543.speaker: TAP agency (Tunisian news agency)
a4543.name: TAP agency (Tunisian news agency)
a4543.speech: Indicates that CAF has announced a solidarity payment of 50,000 dollars for each club that took part in the preliminary rounds of the African interclub competitions, resulting from an agreement signed between CAF and the Association of African Clubs (ACA).

a4543.speaker: CAF (Confederation of African Football)
a4543.name: CAF (Confederation of African Football)
a4543.speech: Announced a solidarity payment of 50,000 dollars for each club having participated in the preliminary rounds of the African interclub competitions.

a4543.speaker: Libyan Express (Libyan outlet)
a4543.name: Libyan Express (Libyan outlet)
a4543.speech: Reveals that USAID has suspended its 50 million dollars in aid and ended its ongoing projects; the American agency notified its partners of its withdrawal from programmes on governance, the fight against disinformation and support for entrepreneurship in the Fezzan, a decision affecting in particular Chemonics International and the French NGO Super-Novae.

a4543.speaker: USAID
a4543.name: USAID
a4543.speech: Notified its partners of its withdrawal from programmes on governance, the fight against disinformation and support for entrepreneurship in the Fezzan.

a4543.speaker: Libya Herald (Libyan outlet)
a4543.name: Libya Herald (Libyan outlet)
a4543.speech: Reports that Akakus Oil has restarted production at the H-46 well with a flow of 650 barrels per day, as part of a strategy to increase the company's production capacity.

a4543.speaker: Ahram (Egyptian newspaper)
a4543.name: Ahram (Egyptian newspaper)
a4543.speech: Revisits the controversy triggered by Ahly club's forfeit in the derby against Zamalek: the club demanded the appointment of foreign referees, a request not met by the Egyptian Federation, which led to the cancellation of the match.

a4543.speaker: Egypt Today (Egyptian outlet)
a4543.name: Egypt Today (Egyptian outlet)
a4543.speech: Specifies that Egypt is targeting between 12 and 15 billion dollars of foreign direct investment by the end of 2025, after a peak of 46.6 billion in 2024, with authorities intending to continue the positive momentum, notably thanks to an improving business climate.

a4581.speaker: Ibrahim Traore, President of Faso, Head of State (inauguration speech delivered by the Minister of Industry, Trade and Handicrafts)
a4581.name: Ibrahim Traore
a4581.title: President of Faso, Head of State (inauguration speech delivered by the Minister of Industry, Trade and Handicrafts)
a4581.speech: Hailed the entrepreneurial boldness of the promoter, who is contributing to the strengthening of the national industrial fabric and who is "in perfect keeping with our ambition to build an autonomous, dynamic and competitive economy" ; said that, in addition to job creation, the CIDF "will reduce our dependence on imports and will contribute to improving our trade balance" ; said the industrial unit "embodies a strong symbol of our capacity to rely on our own resources, our know-how, our ingenuity to build a strong and sovereign economy."

a4581.speaker: Ibrahim Traore, President of Faso, Head of State
a4581.name: Ibrahim Traore
a4581.title: President of Faso, Head of State
a4581.speech: Said he always stands alongside the private sector in order to make it stronger and bolder and to make it a genuine lever of economic growth and social progress: "We will continue to encourage all those who have taken the initiative of embarking on industrialisation. We will support them, help them move forward so that our country becomes industrialised and prosperous."

a4581.speaker: Mady Sawadogo, promoter of the Fassi industrial detergent complex (CIDF)
a4581.name: Mady Sawadogo
a4581.title: promoter of the Fassi industrial detergent complex (CIDF)
a4581.speech: Expressed his gratitude to the President of Faso, Captain Ibrahim Traore, whose "enlightened vision inspires the setting up of structuring projects and, beyond that, the development of the national private sector" for the development of the country.

a4682.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4682.name: Donald Trump
a4682.title: US President
a4682.speech: Said Sunday he is prepared to implement a new phase with additional sanctions on Russia, speaking in the wake of overnight attacks that killed four people and injured dozens in Ukraine; talking to reporters before departing for the US Open tennis final in New York City, answered affirmatively when asked if he was ready to move forward with more sanctions on Russia.

a4682.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4682.name: Donald Trump
a4682.title: US President
a4682.speech: Saying that federal intervention in Chicago would not constitute warfare but rather urban cleanup efforts, despite his social media posting on Chicago alluding to a famous Vietnam War movie.

a4682.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4682.name: Donald Trump
a4682.title: US President
a4682.speech: Asked about embattled Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., described him as “a different kind of a guy” with “a lot of good ideas.”

a4718.speaker: Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA) and African Risk Capacity (ARC) (joint statement)
a4718.name: Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA) and African Risk Capacity (ARC) (joint statement)
a4718.speech: According to a statement from the agencies, this initial phase has already successfully reached 5,705 families residing in the two districts of Jalalaqsi and Bala'ad, addressing their immediate food security needs.

a4856.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a4856.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a4856.speech: Announced the transmission to the National Assembly, for examination and vote, of the draft framework law on construction and housing, stating that it aims to lay down general principles ensuring the quality, safety and durability of buildings, to promote and secure real estate investment, and to take measures favourable to social housing policy; "The ministers concerned are instructed to support its discussion before the National Representation."

a4856.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a4856.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a4856.speech: Stated that it also adopted the decree setting the list of authorities and public officials subject to the obligation to declare their assets, as well as the decree approving the amended statutes of the National Agency for Hospital Maintenance.

a4856.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a4856.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a4856.speech: Gave its agreement for the deployment of 2,431 Aspiring Teachers to the Ministry of Nursery and Primary Education for the 2024-2025 school year, from among the 2,513 candidates who passed the October 2022 test, so that every public primary school class has a teacher.

a4856.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a4856.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a4856.speech: Gave its agreement for contracting with various firms for the diagnostic study, full project management, technical control and delegated contracting authority for the renovation of the former Marriott hotel in Cotonou, a 5-star complex, in order to consolidate the country's supply of high-standard hotel and meeting infrastructure.

a4856.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a4856.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a4856.speech: Authorised contracting for the study of definitive repair works on the sand-retention groyne built under the Millennium Challenge Account and handed to the Autonomous Port of Cotonou in 2011, noting that an independent international expert identified negligence in the design of the infrastructure as the primary cause of its degradation and that the 2014 provisional repair changed nothing, and instructing the ministers concerned to ensure the proper execution of the works.

a4856.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a4856.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a4856.speech: Authorised Benin's participation in the Agricultural Production Show - European Crossroads in Rennes, France (17-19 September 2024), in the 69th session of the International Whaling Commission in Lima, Peru (22-27 September 2024), and the organisation in Cotonou of the second edition of the International Forum on the Living Environment (4-7 October 2024).

a4856.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a4856.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a4856.speech: Pronounced appointments at the Ministry of Energy, Water and Mines on the proposal of the minister, including Alphonse Degnide as Technical Adviser for Water, Michel Ahouansou as Deputy Inspector General of the Ministry, Todeman Flinso Assan as Director General of Energy Planning and Rural Electrification, Achille Adjeniyan as Director General of Hydrocarbons and Other Energy Resources, and departmental directors for Alibori, Atacora, Atlantique, Borgou, Collines, Couffo, Donga, Mono, Oueme, Plateau and Zou.

a4858.speaker: Osama Makkawi, UNICEF Representative to Ghana
a4858.name: Osama Makkawi
a4858.title: UNICEF Representative to Ghana
a4858.speech: Said painting classrooms alongside the students was his first time of doing such an activity.

a4858.speaker: Osama Makkawi, UNICEF Representative to Ghana
a4858.name: Osama Makkawi
a4858.title: UNICEF Representative to Ghana
a4858.speech: In an interview, stated that TVET was the best way to reach the most vulnerable adolescents and young people to impart skills, and emphasised the need to modernise TVET in the 21st century to fit the purpose and the needs of the market and the people.

a4858.speaker: Christin Lucille McConnell, Chair, Development Partners in Education Group (speech read on her behalf by Christopher Nkrumah, education specialist of UNICEF Ghana)
a4858.name: Christin Lucille McConnell
a4858.title: Chair, Development Partners in Education Group (speech read on her behalf by Christopher Nkrumah, education specialist of UNICEF Ghana)
a4858.speech: Said at least in 2024, 242 million students worldwide from pre-primary to upper secondary experienced school disruptions due to climate events, and that in Africa an additional 20 million children were at risk of dropping out of school due to climate-related challenges, highlighting the urgent need to address the intersection of education and climate resilience; said for Ghana approximately 1.2 million children, predominantly in rural areas, were still out of school and vulnerable to risks such as child labour, early marriage and violence, and that climate-induced disruptions in 2023, including flooding that affected over 30,000 children and heatwave that rendered classrooms uncomfortable, further underscored the need for action ; "We are particularly optimistic about Ghana's potential to address these challenges through home-grown solutions. TVET institutions stand out as strategic partners in championing innovative approaches to solving problems in schools, workplaces and communities. By leveraging their expertise, we can design and implement climate-smart and disaster-resilient learning facilities, while addressing broader infrastructural and environmental challenges" ; urged all stakeholders including the government, development partners, private sector and community members to take concrete actions to strengthen partnerships between TVET and non-TVET institutions to address infrastructural and environmental challenges effectively.

a4858.speaker: Dr Eric Kofi Adzroe, Director of Infrastructural Planning and Development at the Ghana TVET Service
a4858.name: Dr Eric Kofi Adzroe
a4858.title: Director of Infrastructural Planning and Development at the Ghana TVET Service
a4858.speech: Called on parents to encourage their children to take the path of TVET for the nation to develop.

a4858.speaker: Awo Yaa Otwiwa, queen mother of Agyemanti
a4858.name: Awo Yaa Otwiwa
a4858.title: queen mother of Agyemanti
a4858.speech: Said education held the key to improving the lives of their children such that going forward, it would be difficult for one to get a good employment opportunity if one was not educated.

a4858.speaker: Elizabeth Afriyie, Akuapem South Municipal Director of Education
a4858.name: Elizabeth Afriyie
a4858.title: Akuapem South Municipal Director of Education
a4858.speech: Called on all to work together to ensure that every child had access to quality education and the opportunity to reach their full learning potential.

a5058.speaker: Ibrahim Karaosmanoglu, mayor of Kocaeli province, Turkey
a5058.name: Ibrahim Karaosmanoglu
a5058.title: mayor of Kocaeli province, Turkey
a5058.speech: Said: “Through the ‘trees bearing books’ event we wanted to draw attention to the largest book fair in Turkey and to encourage the rising generation to read, for a better future for the country.”

a5058.speaker: Daily Sabah (Turkish newspaper)
a5058.name: Daily Sabah (Turkish newspaper)
a5058.speech: Reported that books of old and modern Turkish literature were placed inside bags and hung on the branches of old trees near the book fair that opened in the province last Saturday and runs until 22 May, which astonished passers-by and students.

a5138.speaker: Daily News (US publication)
a5138.name: Daily News (US publication)
a5138.speech: According to the Daily News, the American president was not entirely fair if his aim was to prevent terrorists from coming onto American territory: in consulting the list, the site realized that President Trump does not do business with the countries chosen, whereas other countries whose nationals have already carried out terrorist attacks causing nearly 3,000 victims on American soil — notably Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkey — were spared; the site noted that President Trump's companies have enormous financial interests in these three countries.

a5138.speaker: Several organizations (unnamed)
a5138.name: Several organizations (unnamed)
a5138.speech: Cried scandal since the announcement of the 7 countries concerned by the temporary visa ban measure.

a5175.speaker: Bingquan Zhou, Managing Director of China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (Malawi) Limited (CCECC)
a5175.name: Bingquan Zhou
a5175.title: Managing Director of China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (Malawi) Limited (CCECC)
a5175.speech: Explains that he has been in Malawi for so many years now and has overseen a lot of projects in road construction, water supply and building construction — “which have earned praise from clients, authorities and the public.”

a5175.speaker: Bingquan Zhou, Managing Director of CCECC Malawi
a5175.name: Bingquan Zhou
a5175.title: Managing Director of CCECC Malawi
a5175.speech: On the company profile: “China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation, formerly known as the Foreign Aid Bureau of the Ministry of Railways of China, is a leading international contractor under China Railway Construction Corporation (CRCC) — one of the ‘Fortune Global 500’ companies. It was established with the approval of the State Council in 1979 and has grown into one of the top-tier Chinese companies in the international project contracting industry. Since the construction of the Tanzania-Zambia Railway, China's largest foreign aid project in the 1960s, CCECC has experienced rapid growth. It has been ranked among the top 100 companies on the ENR Top 250 International Contractors list for 20 years in a row... Currently, CCECC has permanent offices, branch companies, or ongoing projects in over 110 countries and regions.”

a5175.speaker: Bingquan Zhou, Managing Director of CCECC Malawi
a5175.name: Bingquan Zhou
a5175.title: Managing Director of CCECC Malawi
a5175.speech: On projects in Malawi: “Our current projects in Malawi mainly include, but not limit to, upgrading of Lirangwe-Chipini (S139); road & rehabilitation of Kaphatenga-Dwangwa Road in Nkhotakota, just to name a few.” ; “Rehabilitation of Kaphatenga-Dwangwa Road, funded by Africa Development Bank (AfDB), OPEC and Malawi Government, commenced at the beginning of June, 2025 with two years contract duration. Upgrading of Lirangwe-Chipini (S139) Road, with government funding, commenced in April, 2025 with 18 months duration.”

a5175.speaker: Bingquan Zhou, Managing Director of CCECC Malawi
a5175.name: Bingquan Zhou
a5175.title: Managing Director of CCECC Malawi
a5175.speech: On the labour market: “We have 443 local Malawian employees at present, and 800 local employees during peak construction periods, most of who receive our companies' systematic training — such as land surveying, work designing, contractual management, and OSH management, while unskilled laboring in steel fixing, civil works, concreting works and carpentry works.”

a5175.speaker: Bingquan Zhou, Managing Director of CCECC Malawi
a5175.name: Bingquan Zhou
a5175.title: Managing Director of CCECC Malawi
a5175.speech: On successes and challenges: “We have successfully conducted and completed a lot of projects in various categories, such as water supply system, road construction and building construction — which have greatly improved the living standard of Malawian people.” He noted the Nkhata Bay Town water supply system was completed in July 2023 and commissioned by President Dr. Lazarus Chakwera, whose quality and progress have been praised by his Excellency, and that the Kenyatta Road and Sharrar Street contract was awarded the ‘Outstanding Civil Project Award’ during the inaugural Malawi National Construction Day on May 20, 2025.

a5175.speaker: Bingquan Zhou, Managing Director of CCECC Malawi
a5175.name: Bingquan Zhou
a5175.title: Managing Director of CCECC Malawi
a5175.speech: On corporate social responsibility: said that by undertaking projects, it creates job opportunities and cultivates technical talents for the local community, bringing real benefits to local people; the Nkhata Bay Town water supply system employed approximately more than 1,200 local employees and provided them systematic training, and upon completion provides clean water for nearly 100,000 residents.

a5175.speaker: Bingquan Zhou, Managing Director of CCECC Malawi
a5175.name: Bingquan Zhou
a5175.title: Managing Director of CCECC Malawi
a5175.speech: On partners and regional presence: named EMMAC Construction Limited, Leonor Engineering Limited and Master Road Construction as partners in Malawi, and said the company is also in Zambia, Mozambique, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Botswana, Namibia, Kenya, Tanzania, Nigeria and Ethiopia, among other countries.

a5175.speaker: Bingquan Zhou, Managing Director of CCECC Malawi
a5175.name: Bingquan Zhou
a5175.title: Managing Director of CCECC Malawi
a5175.speech: Last word: “Malawi enjoys political stability and maintains a relatively fast economic growth. We are fully confident in Malawi's future development. China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation has the ability and confidence to deliver low-carbon, environmentally friendly, green, safe and high-quality projects to the people of Malawi and will try our best to contribute to the country's infrastructure construction.”

a5501.speaker: Chargee d'affaires of the Embassy of the United States of America in Benin
a5501.name: Chargee d'affaires of the Embassy of the United States of America in Benin
a5501.speech: Said, on the occasion of the third anniversary of the programme's implementation in October 2009: “The MCA BENIN programme is the best in the world among all the programmes benefiting from Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) resources, in terms of transparency in financial management, procurement and the quality of the leadership of its Coordinator.”

a5501.speaker: Semi-annual financial audits of the MCA-BENIN programme
a5501.name: Semi-annual financial audits of the MCA-BENIN programme
a5501.speech: All the semi-annual financial audits carried out since the programme's implementation revealed no case of malfeasance or embezzlement.

a5501.speaker: Minister in charge of the Maritime Economy, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the MCA
a5501.name: Minister in charge of the Maritime Economy
a5501.title: Chairman of the Board of Directors of the MCA
a5501.speech: Introduced new fees at the Port of Cotonou, and, after a threat from the Americans, was obliged on 30 March 2010 to take three decisions suspending the implementation of the orders establishing the new fees.

a5501.speaker: Investigating judge in the Simon Pierre Adovelande case (court record)
a5501.name: Investigating judge in the Simon Pierre Adovelande case (court record)
a5501.speech: Ordered his release as of 1 April 2010.

a5501.speaker: Public Prosecutor's Office (Parquet) of Benin
a5501.name: Public Prosecutor's Office (Parquet) of Benin
a5501.speech: Is demanding one billion CFA francs in bail for his provisional release in a disputed case worth 360 million CFA francs, and appealed against the investigating judge's release order.

a5577.speaker: Bruno Ching’andu, TAZARA Chief Executive Officer
a5577.name: Bruno Ching’andu
a5577.title: TAZARA Chief Executive Officer
a5577.speech: Announced during the Zambia International Mining and Energy Conference (ZIMEC 2025) in Kitwe, Zambia that investment negotiations are in their final stages and that with CCECC’s $1.4 billion investment the company will operate TAZARA for 30 years ; “The investment from CCECC will not only restore our railway infrastructure but also position TAZARA as a key enabler of trade and economic growth between Tanzania and Zambia.”

a5674.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
a5674.name: Filipe Nyusi
a5674.title: Mozambican President
a5674.speech: Declared on Thursday that no elephants have been poached since 2018 in the Niassa Special Reserve, the largest conservation area in the country: “The investments and the legal reforms we have been undertaking in the conservation areas have brought a new dynamic and important gains for the Reserve” ; added that the increase in the number of partners, and “the healthy coexistence between the various operators, alongside the government and the communities” had also contributed to a healthy environment for the development of the Reserve.

a5674.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
a5674.name: Filipe Nyusi
a5674.title: Mozambican President
a5674.speech: Thanked the defence and security forces for their cooperation with the Niassa rangers.

a5674.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
a5674.name: Filipe Nyusi
a5674.title: Mozambican President
a5674.speech: “The Mozambican state will continue to do its part by investing in a programme of monitoring, through placing collars and satellite tracking of the iconic animals of the Reserve, ensuring their continued protection and the integrity of their habitats” ; “This is a re-affirmation of our commitment to the conservation of biodiversity, and of emblematic species in particular. This is an activity we promise to follow and to honour, in defence of our entire planet, our collective home.”

a5674.speaker: Helen Pataki, director in Mozambique of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a5674.name: Helen Pataki
a5674.title: director in Mozambique of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a5674.speech: Said that American support had played a determinant role in the fight against poaching: “Support from the US Government’s Aerial Vigilance Programme has allowed monitoring, and also the deployment of patrols” ; “This has led to a reduction in the cases of illegal mining and logging in the reserve, as well as cutting to zero the poaching of elephants since 2018” ; stressed that the preservation of biodiversity is a necessity in a world facing the threats of climate change and environmental degradation.

a5712.speaker: Namibian Ministry of Health (government announcement)
a5712.name: Namibian Ministry of Health (government announcement)
a5712.speech: Announced the launch of the trusted travel system in the country recently, which means passengers intending to travel to Namibia are expected to visit any of the trusted travel accredited laboratories for a polymerase chain reaction (PCR) Covid-19 test.

a5712.speaker: Ben Nangombe, Executive Director of the Namibian Ministry of Health
a5712.name: Ben Nangombe
a5712.title: Executive Director of the Namibian Ministry of Health
a5712.speech: "The transition period has been extended from 1 December 2021 to 15 January 2022 to allow for a smooth transition, especially given many anticipated travels during the festive season." ; Said after 15 January 2022, only Covid-19 certificates obtained on the trusted travel platform or verified on the global haven system will be valid for exit or entry into Namibia at the Impalila Island border post.

a5712.speaker: Ben Nangombe, Executive Director of the Namibian Ministry of Health
a5712.name: Ben Nangombe
a5712.title: Executive Director of the Namibian Ministry of Health
a5712.speech: "The ministry appreciates the cooperation and input received from the public and concerned industries in perfecting the TT system as an intervention to curb potential importation of positive Copvid-19 cases in Namibia."

a5878.speaker: Mayaki (speaker at the Africa-China Forum on Agri-Tech and Industrial Cooperation)
a5878.name: Mayaki (speaker at the Africa-China Forum on Agri-Tech and Industrial Cooperation)
a5878.speech: "We can leverage China's successes in agricultural modernization, rural transformation and poverty alleviation as reference points for Africa's own agricultural renaissance, while recognizing the specificity of African ecosystems and cultures"; stressed that joint research between China and Africa in climate-smart farming practices, development of high-yielding crops, modern irrigation technologies and digital extension services could offer lasting solution to hunger, rural poverty and malnutrition affecting the continent.

a5878.speaker: Hamadi Boga, Vice President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a5878.name: Hamadi Boga
a5878.title: Vice President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a5878.speech: Noted that China has set the pace in technology- and innovation-led agricultural modernization, inspiring African nations to follow suit, feed their growing population and leapfrog into an industrial era; said Sino-African agricultural cooperation has rapidly evolved as witnessed by technology transfer, establishment of demonstration zones, exchange visits and institutional collaboration, boosting crop yield, agro-processing and exports; called on African research institutions to forge long-term partnership with their Chinese counterparts to accelerate an inclusive food systems transformation, rooted in improved soil health, climate resilience, access to finance, technologies and markets.

a5878.speaker: Guo Haiyan, Chinese Ambassador to Kenya
a5878.name: Guo Haiyan
a5878.title: Chinese Ambassador to Kenya
a5878.speech: Said China is keen to share with Africa's bilateral partners its home-grown technologies, innovations, experience and best practices, which could hasten the continent's agricultural modernization to realize food security and boost export competitiveness; noted that China-Africa agricultural cooperation has prioritized technology transfer, facilitating trade in agricultural commodities and upgrading value chains for farm produce, and added that China has partnered with African countries to enhance response to crop pests and diseases, capacity building for extension workers and farmers, and deployment of technologies for scaling up agro-processing and value addition.

a5920.speaker: Darren Welch, British Ambassador to Ethiopia
a5920.name: Darren Welch
a5920.title: British Ambassador to Ethiopia
a5920.speech: Urged all stakeholders to redouble efforts towards the humanitarian cause of the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS), underlining that the humanitarian effort needs more support from ambassadors, humanitarian leaders, government officials and members of the civil society ; "This year we'll give perhaps 80 million pounds in support of humanitarian relief in Ethiopia as part of our desire to remain a steadfast and strong partner of the Ethiopian and the UN humanitarian system in the country," Welch pledged during an exclusive interview with EBC World.

a5920.speaker: Ervin Massinga, US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a5920.name: Ervin Massinga
a5920.title: US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a5920.speech: Underscored that efforts should be redoubled to commit to the people, who are vulnerable around the world and here in Ethiopia.

a5920.speaker: Abera Tola, President of the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS)
a5920.name: Abera Tola
a5920.title: President of the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS)
a5920.speech: “Our volunteers have been with communities in their most difficult times—offering help, hope, and healing” ; “Their courage and compassion reflect the very essence of this year’s theme. Today’s celebration is not just ceremonial, it is a recognition of their daily sacrifices” ; called on development partners, supporters, and the public to renew their commitment by backing the Society’s fundraising drives, ensuring the safety of humanitarian workers, and expanding outreach to vulnerable populations.

a5973.speaker: Xi Jinping, President of China (letter of congratulations to the Forum)
a5973.name: Xi Jinping
a5973.title: President of China (letter of congratulations to the Forum)
a5973.speech: Stressed that achieving lasting peace and universal security was a shared aspiration of the Chinese and African peoples, and that China was ready to work with African friends to build a China-Africa community with a shared future in the new era.

a5973.speaker: General Wei Fenghe, State Councillor and Minister of National Defence of China
a5973.name: General Wei Fenghe
a5973.title: State Councillor and Minister of National Defence of China
a5973.speech: In his thematic address, stated that China and Africa should, in keeping with the spirit of China-Africa friendship and cooperation, implement the Global Security Initiative and advance toward the fine vision of jointly building a security community for all ; according to him, China and Africa must maintain close strategic communication, strengthen their cooperation in equipment and technology, deepen joint maritime training and exercises, and broaden exchanges in the professional field, in order to promote China-Africa cooperation on peace and security in a deeper and more substantial way.

a5973.speaker: Hu Bin, Ambassador of China to Djibouti
a5973.name: Hu Bin
a5973.title: Ambassador of China to Djibouti
a5973.speech: Described the 2nd China-Africa Forum for Peace and Security, held on 25 July by videoconference with 50 ministerial-level representatives and senior officials from African countries and the African Union, and said the parties held in-depth discussions on the theme "Strengthening Solidarity and Cooperation to Achieve Common Security" ; said China has always maintained that Africa is a stage for international cooperation, not an arena for competition between major powers, and that on the basis of respect for the will of African countries, non-interference in their internal affairs and the basic norms governing international relations, China actively and constructively supports African countries' efforts to preserve peace and security ; said that faced with a turbulent international situation President Xi Jinping put forward the Global Security Initiative, China's solution to international security challenges and a guide for China-Africa security cooperation, and that China has also proposed the Initiative for Peaceful Development in the Horn of Africa ; said that in the future China will continue to develop exchanges and dialogues with Djibouti and all African countries in the fields of peace and security, upholding the principle that Africans solve Africa's problems in their own way, supporting the leading role of African countries and the AU in the region's peace and security affairs, and encouraging their efforts to promote peace and stability and combat terrorism.

a5973.speaker: Hu Bin, Ambassador of China to Djibouti
a5973.name: Hu Bin
a5973.title: Ambassador of China to Djibouti
a5973.speech: Said that over the past 95 years, under the leadership of the Communist Party of China, the People's Liberation Army has accomplished remarkable feats for the independence and renewal of the Chinese nation, and that guided by President Xi Jinping's military strategy of the new era, the modernisation of China's defence and Army continues to progress ; said the PLA has always been an unshakeable force for world peace, providing the international community with security public goods such as UN-mandated peacekeeping, counter-piracy operations and humanitarian assistance; that among the five permanent members of the UN Security Council China is the largest contributor of troops to peacekeeping missions, having sent nearly 50,000 military personnel to 25 missions with about 80% deployed in Africa; and that the Chinese Navy has deployed 41 flotillas in the Gulf of Aden since 2008 and escorted more than 7,000 Chinese and foreign vessels.

a5973.speaker: Hu Bin, Ambassador of China to Djibouti
a5973.name: Hu Bin
a5973.title: Ambassador of China to Djibouti
a5973.speech: Said the Chinese Support Base stationed in Djibouti is an important foothold for the Chinese Army in its counter-piracy and UN-mandated peacekeeping operations, that Djibouti's firm support is indispensable to the Base's construction and operation, and that China greatly appreciates the valuable support of the Djiboutian government under the leadership of Mr. Ismail Omar Guelleh ; said the Djiboutian Armed Forces are recognised by China and other members of the international community for their achievements in supporting international anti-piracy operations and the fight against maritime criminal activities and regional terrorism, and that 2,000 Djiboutian officers and soldiers are on permanent alert to fight terrorists and defend regional stability ; said the outlook for the strategic partnership between China and Djibouti is promising and that China intends to continue strengthening strategic mutual trust with Djibouti, to support it in playing a greater role in regional and international affairs, to support as far as possible the strengthening of Djibouti's national defence capabilities, and to promote cooperation in various fields, including peace and security, at a higher level.

a5973.speaker: Said Nouh Hassan, Minister of the Interior of the Republic of Djibouti
a5973.name: Said Nouh Hassan
a5973.title: Minister of the Interior of the Republic of Djibouti
a5973.speech: Said in his address that the Forum would create new momentum for the development of the comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership between China and Africa, and make new contributions to Africa's sustainable development and to the promotion of peace, stability, development and prosperity in the world in the post-epidemic era.

a5973.speaker: Representatives of African countries
a5973.name: Representatives of African countries
a5973.speech: Expressed their willingness to strengthen solidarity and cooperation with China and to make active contributions to building a China-Africa community with a shared future.

a5996.speaker: World Bank, World Health Organization (WHO) and UN Children's Fund (UNICEF)
a5996.name: World Bank
a5996.title: World Health Organization (WHO) and UN Children's Fund (UNICEF)
a5996.speech: Signed a US$ 82 million agreement to improve access to critical health services for more than 8 million vulnerable people across Sudan and strengthen the health system.

a5996.speaker: Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF)
a5996.name: Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF)
a5996.speech: "Strongly condemns ongoing violent attacks on patients and staff at Bashair Teaching hospital, located in a Rapid Support Forces-controlled area of Khartoum, Sudan. Despite extensive engagements with all stakeholders, these attacks have continued."

a5996.speaker: Aid workers caught up in the five-month siege of El Fasher
a5996.name: Aid workers caught up in the five-month siege of El Fasher
a5996.speech: Said the lack of services and escalating violence was making life harder by the day, calling for immediate action to protect those at risk.

a5996.speaker: Radhouane Nouicer, designated Expert on Sudan of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a5996.name: Radhouane Nouicer
a5996.title: designated Expert on Sudan of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a5996.speech: Called for the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and their respective allied armed movements and militia to take immediate measures to ensure protection.

a5996.speaker: Nutrition screening by Sudanese health authorities and Medecins Sans Frontieres in Zamzam camp, North Darfur
a5996.name: Nutrition screening by Sudanese health authorities and Medecins Sans Frontieres in Zamzam camp
a5996.title: North Darfur
a5996.speech: The results indicate that malnutrition is only getting worse. "Without supplies, we have been forced to reduce our services."

a5996.speaker: IGAD Regional Focus of the 2024 Global Report on Food Crises
a5996.name: IGAD Regional Focus of the 2024 Global Report on Food Crises
a5996.speech: Highlights a worsening food insecurity crisis in the IGAD region, which includes Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda.

a5996.speaker: IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (ICPAC)
a5996.name: IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (ICPAC)
a5996.speech: Has released its seasonal forecast for October to December 2024, indicating drier-than-normal conditions in the eastern Horn of Africa, while western regions are likely to experience above-normal rainfall.

a5996.speaker: Amnesty International (latest briefing)
a5996.name: Amnesty International (latest briefing)
a5996.speech: Highlights how a continuous influx of weapons is exacerbating the conflict in Sudan, leading to severe civilian suffering.

a6120.speaker: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) (latest data/analysis)
a6120.name: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) (latest data/analysis)
a6120.speech: According to its latest data, conflict and rising food prices are plunging the Democratic Republic of Congo into one of the world's worst food crises, bringing the number of people in acute hunger to 28 million (IPC Phase 3 and above), an increase of 2.5 million since last December's violence, of whom 3.9 million face emergency hunger (IPC Phase 4).

a6120.speaker: UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and World Food Programme (WFP)
a6120.name: UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and World Food Programme (WFP)
a6120.speech: Revealed that the number of people in acute food insecurity in the DRC has reached an unprecedented level, according to the most recent IPC analysis; called on the international community to increase funding and humanitarian access to avert a large-scale catastrophe, warning that without immediate aid hunger will continue to rise.

a6120.speaker: Eric Perdison, WFP Regional Director for Southern Africa and interim WFP Country Director in the DRC
a6120.name: Eric Perdison
a6120.title: WFP Regional Director for Southern Africa and interim WFP Country Director in the DRC
a6120.speech: “The humanitarian situation in the DRC is deteriorating rapidly. Families already in difficulty are now facing even more severe conditions.” ; “We have restarted our operations in some areas of North and South Kivu, but we urgently need additional resources.”

a6120.speaker: Athman Mravili, interim FAO Representative
a6120.name: Athman Mravili
a6120.title: interim FAO Representative
a6120.speech: “The situation is catastrophic: harvests are lost, food prices are soaring and millions of people are in acute food insecurity, becoming increasingly vulnerable.” Adding: “We need more resources to support sustainable livelihoods for the displaced. We aim to help 1.6 million people in the provinces of North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri and Tanganyika.”

a6264.speaker: Tony Hinchcliffe, comedian (who goes by the name Kill Tony)
a6264.name: Tony Hinchcliffe
a6264.title: comedian (who goes by the name Kill Tony)
a6264.speech: “There's a lot going on. I don't know if you know this but there's literally a floating island of garbage in the middle of the ocean right now. I think it's called Puerto Rico.” ; He also suggested Latinos “loved making babies”, and made a comment about black people and watermelons – drawing on a racist trope.

a6264.speaker: A Trump adviser
a6264.name: A Trump adviser
a6264.speech: Distanced the Republican from the Puerto Rico joke.

a6264.speaker: Maria Elvira Salazar, US congresswoman (post on X)
a6264.name: Maria Elvira Salazar
a6264.title: US congresswoman (post on X)
a6264.speech: Said she was “disgusted” by the “racist comment”, said it did not “reflect the GOP values”, and noted the thousands of Puerto Ricans who served in the military.

a6264.speaker: Rick Scott, US Senator (post on X)
a6264.name: Rick Scott
a6264.title: US Senator (post on X)
a6264.speech: “The joke bombed for a reason. It's not funny and it's not true.” He added that “Puerto Ricans are amazing people and amazing Americans.”

a6264.speaker: David Rem, childhood friend of Trump
a6264.name: David Rem
a6264.title: childhood friend of Trump

a6264.speaker: Rudy Giuliani, Trump's former lawyer
a6264.name: Rudy Giuliani
a6264.title: Trump's former lawyer
a6264.speech: Falsely claimed the Democratic candidate was “on the side of the terrorists” in the war in the Gaza conflict.

a6264.speaker: Donald Trump
a6264.name: Donald Trump
a6264.speech: Used the occasion to announce a plan for tax credits for those who take care of a parent or a loved one: “It's about time that they were recognised”; he also reiterated plans for a mass deportation for illegal migrants, speaking of his wish to “rescue” places that had been “invaded and conquered” by “vicious and bloodthirsty criminals”.

a6264.speaker: The Harris campaign
a6264.name: The Harris campaign
a6264.speech: Said the language at the rally was “divisive and demeaning”.

a6264.speaker: Bad Bunny, Puerto Rican rapper
a6264.name: Bad Bunny
a6264.title: Puerto Rican rapper
a6264.speech: Endorsed Harris for president, posting multiple videos of Harris talking about the island, her ideas to help residents, and her attacks on how Trump handled Hurricane Maria as president; his comments appeared to be pre-planned, and he did not address the remarks by Mr Hinchcliffe.

a6264.speaker: A source close to Bad Bunny (anonymous)
a6264.name: A source close to Bad Bunny (anonymous)
a6264.speech: Confirmed to the BBC's US partner, CBS News, that this represented an endorsement of Harris, breaking his longstanding tradition of not weighing in on national politics.

a6264.speaker: Ricky Martin, Puerto Rican singer
a6264.name: Ricky Martin
a6264.title: Puerto Rican singer
a6264.speech: Told his fans “this is what they think of us” and urged them to vote for Harris.

a6264.speaker: Pew Research Centre
a6264.name: Pew Research Centre
a6264.speech: According to the Pew Research centre, there are around 36 million Hispanic voters eligible to vote this year.

a6264.speaker: Mike Shapiro, Trump supporter visiting New York from New Jersey
a6264.name: Mike Shapiro
a6264.title: Trump supporter visiting New York from New Jersey
a6264.speech: “I hear people say he's fascist, fascist, racist, racist, racist” ; “But I see a lot of diversity. I see everybody, all nationalities. And even here, I met a lot of blacks, a lot of Latino, a lot of Asians. The tide is changing a bit.”

a6264.speaker: Mike Boatman, rally attendee (said it was his 18th Trump rally)
a6264.name: Mike Boatman
a6264.title: rally attendee (said it was his 18th Trump rally)
a6264.speech: “He's having rallies where people don't expect him to have rallies because I think more people – people who didn't like him – are seeing that Donald Trump was a good president” ; “They've had four years of Trump and four years of Biden, and Kamala is just an extension of Biden, and they can compare and they know when they were better off.”

a6362.speaker: UN human rights office (OHCHR) reports
a6362.name: UN human rights office (OHCHR) reports
a6362.speech: There are reports reaching the UN human rights office (OHCHR) of summary executions of civilians trying to escape the violence in El Fasher, some of it ethnically motivated. The reports say the killings are mostly committed by the Rapid Support Forces, targeting former combatants who have put down their weapons. Graphic reports said RSF had summarily executed five men who were attempting to bring food supplies into the Darfuri regional capital, which has been blockaded by the militia for 18 months. They were accused of supporting the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF).

a6362.speaker: Volker Türk, UN human rights chief
a6362.name: Volker Türk
a6362.title: UN human rights chief
a6362.speech: “The risk of further large-scale, ethnically motivated violations and atrocities in El Fasher is mounting by the day,” warned UN human rights chief Volker Türk, who said urgent and concrete action is needed to ensure the protection of civilians in El Fasher and safe passage for those trying to leave. ; Mr. Türk enjoined RSF commanders to an obligation under international law to protect civilians and ensure the safe passage of humanitarian assistance.

a6362.speaker: António Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a6362.name: António Guterres
a6362.title: UN Secretary-General
a6362.speech: has told journalists that the “terrible escalation” necessitates the international community to exert pressure on countries taking sides in Sudan’s internal conflict by “providing weapons” to one of the warring sides, urging them to agree a ceasefire.

a6362.speaker: Denise Brown, UN humanitarian coordinator for Sudan
a6362.name: Denise Brown
a6362.title: UN humanitarian coordinator for Sudan
a6362.speech: at a press briefing on Monday said civilians including adults and children fleeing El Fasher often appear “dehydrated, malnourished, some injured and all traumatised.”

a6362.speaker: United Nations / Denise Brown, UN humanitarian coordinator for Sudan
a6362.name: United Nations / Denise Brown
a6362.title: UN humanitarian coordinator for Sudan
a6362.speech: According to the UN some 130 aid workers have been killed since the conflict erupted more than two years ago, with reports of volunteers being killed in El Fasher, Ms. Brown said. “These people are the backbone of the humanitarian response in the most difficult areas and they are also protected under international humanitarian law,” she added.

a6468.speaker: Jonathan Richter, USAID resident representative in Benin
a6468.name: Jonathan Richter
a6468.title: USAID resident representative in Benin
a6468.speech: At the fair’s opening ceremony, set out the reasons for the session: said his agency’s creed is to support countries’ efforts to reduce extreme poverty and consolidate their democracies; said that in Benin USAID’s programmes are focused specifically on the health sector in order to reduce the number of avoidable deaths; explained that the aim of this strategic choice is to enable the local population to live a long, productive life for the country’s growth and prosperity.

a6468.speaker: Lucien Toko, chief of staff of the Minister of Health of Benin
a6468.name: Lucien Toko
a6468.title: chief of staff of the Minister of Health of Benin
a6468.speech: After praising the initiative, recalled that Benin intends to have a completely transformed health system with better universal health coverage by 2020 or 2021: “We requested and obtained USAID’s support to develop mobile applications in the area of maternal and child health care in order to reach this objective” ; considers that information and communication technologies constitute an important lever to support the continuous and sustainable improvement of the health sector.

a6485.speaker: Retired Nigerian soldier (anonymous)
a6485.name: Retired Nigerian soldier (anonymous)
a6485.speech: Alleged that the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) funded Boko Haram terrorists in Nigeria and that the US and UK governments sabotaged Goodluck Jonathan’s administration in collaboration with the APC: “In respect of this news trending about USAID, some of the funds raised for Africa were being used to fund Boko Haram.”

a6485.speaker: Retired Nigerian soldier (anonymous)
a6485.name: Retired Nigerian soldier (anonymous)
a6485.speech: Claimed that former President Muhammadu Buhari’s administration and the All Progressives Congress (APC) undermined the fight against Boko Haram during former President Goodluck Jonathan’s government, allowing the terrorists to gain the upper hand against the armed forces; stated that Jonathan’s administration had made significant progress against Boko Haram with the help of foreign machinery from Ukraine, Russia and retired soldiers from the United States, but that when Buhari took office he halted the foreign support, allowing Boko Haram to regroup and rearm: “So, some of the experts were retired soldiers from the US but they worked with a private company. They managed to bring them to train 72 Airborne battalion. Immediately Buhari became the President, he stopped those guys and asked them to go back, stating that he did not want any foreign soldier on Nigerian soil.” ; “As at that time, we had already started pushing those terrorists far and we had the upper hand ahead of the 2015 election. But after President Buhari won the election, he sent those guys back and they provided mines that could destroy those tanks that were brought from Russia. They gave them anti-tank that can destroy those tanks.” ; “So those guys (terrorists) started using those weapons against Nigerian Army which gave them (Boko Haram) the upper hand.” ; “Many of the generals who spoke, telling them the situation on the ground were either moved away or withdrawn. We believe there was sabotage from even the government for the army not to succeed. How many are Boko Haram terrorists if it is not the government sponsoring them, giving them information and using them against the army?” ; “Even when this kidnapping issue started in Kaduna, what happened? At the end of the day, they swapped those detainees with prisoners in Kuje Correctional Centre. The government knew what they were doing.”

a6485.speaker: Retired Nigerian soldier (anonymous)
a6485.name: Retired Nigerian soldier (anonymous)
a6485.speech: Provided details on how the Jonathan administration had acquired T-75 tanks from Ukraine and Russia, transported them to South Africa where Nigerian soldiers were trained to operate them, and how the APC allegedly informed the US and South African governments about the transaction, leading to the seizure of the plane (Pastor Ayo Oritsejafor’s) used to transport the funds: “First of all, when Goodluck Jonathan was in power and we needed support from the US and Britain, they denied us, and Goodluck had to go to Ukraine and Russia to get all these T-75 tanks.” ; “Those tanks arrived in South Africa and the Nigerian Army could not operate them so they had to come with experts - retired soldiers there to teach Nigerian soldiers how to handle the tanks. They got all those things at their black-market level there.” ; “The point there is this, those guys requested for money, that they had to be paid six months arrears before going to Borno so that they could teach our soldiers. And it was not in naira, it was in dollars.” ; “They required Nigerian government to pay them there (in South Africa) so that they could teach us one or two things because we would get the equipment.” ; “The APC even went to South Africa, even when the government of Nigeria was telling the government of South Africa that it was about security matter, that it was not something to be exposed.” ; “They (APC) just used it to frustrate us (soldiers) in the battle in North-East Nigeria. The government was not going to use the weapons against the people of Nigeria.”

a6485.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman (Republican, Pennsylvania)
a6485.name: Scott Perry
a6485.title: US Congressman (Republican, Pennsylvania)
a6485.speech: Recently claimed that USAID had funded terrorist organisations, including Boko Haram, during the inaugural hearing of the Subcommittee on Delivering on Government Efficiency on 14 February 2025: “Who gets some of that money? Does that name ring a bell to anybody in the room? Because your money, your money, $697 million annually, plus the shipments of cash funds in Madrasas, ISIS, Al-Qaeda, Boko Haram, ISIS Khorasan, terrorist training camps. That’s what it’s funding.”

a6485.speaker: Pastor Ayo Oritsejafor
a6485.name: Pastor Ayo Oritsejafor
a6485.speech: Admitted owning the jet but denied any involvement or knowledge of the arms deal; stated that the aircraft was a gift from his congregation and ministry partners and that he had leased it to another party at the time.

a6485.speaker: Nigerian government
a6485.name: Nigerian government
a6485.speech: Insisted that the funds were for a security matter and should not have been exposed.

a6594.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ghana
a6594.name: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa
a6594.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ghana
a6594.speech: Has called for Africa to take charge of its own development and seek homegrown solutions to its challenges; speaking on TV3's Key Points programme, stressed the need for greater unity among African nations and a shift away from dependence on foreign aid; highlighted the impact of global geopolitical shifts, particularly the Russia-Ukraine conflict and changes in US foreign policy, on Africa's economic stability, noting that traditional partners including the European Union and the United States are reducing aid and shifting priorities, leaving Africa vulnerable: "African nations must realise that at the end of the day, we cannot continue to rely on external aid. The only way forward is to take our destiny into our own hands and ensure that our policies and trade agreements benefit Africans first."

a6594.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ghana
a6594.name: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa
a6594.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ghana
a6594.speech: Criticised what he described as the "inward-looking" policies of some African nations, warning that excessive protectionism hinders the continent's collective growth, and advocated the harmonisation of trade policies to foster regional cooperation and economic integration: "We cannot have some countries believing that because they have larger markets, they can go it alone. If we all come together and commit to a shared vision, we can build a sustainable and prosperous Africa."

a6594.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ghana
a6594.name: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa
a6594.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ghana
a6594.speech: Further stressed the importance of resource management, pointing out that Africa is blessed with abundant natural wealth yet agreements in the extractive sector often benefit external entities more than the continent's citizens, and called for stronger negotiations to ensure Africa's resources serve its people: "We must change the paradigm so that our resources work in the interest of our people. It is time to put Africa's welfare at the centre of our foreign relations."

a6682.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) 2024 biennial report on the state of school feeding worldwide
a6682.name: World Food Programme (WFP) 2024 biennial report on the state of school feeding worldwide
a6682.speech: According to the report, twenty million additional children in sub-Saharan Africa are benefiting from school meals compared with 2022; sub-Saharan Africa is the region that recorded the strongest progress, rising from 66 million children served in 2022 to 87 million in 2024, an increase of more than 30%; Benin, alongside Botswana, Burkina Faso, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, Rwanda and Zambia, is among the countries that finance their programmes mainly from national budgets; direct purchases from smallholder farmers jumped by 800% in two years, benefiting more than 23,000 producers; countries such as Chad, Ethiopia, Madagascar and Rwanda have multiplied by six the number of pupils receiving school meals since 2022; in Burundi local sourcing increased farmers' incomes by 50% and created jobs in 67 cooperatives; and in Malawi every dollar invested in school meals generates eight dollars in economic benefits.

a6682.speaker: Eric Perdison, WFP Regional Director for Eastern and Southern Africa
a6682.name: Eric Perdison
a6682.title: WFP Regional Director for Eastern and Southern Africa
a6682.speech: "A meal at school is more than simply feeding a child. It is also an investment in the family, the community and, ultimately, the future of the country."

a6682.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6682.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6682.speech: Reaffirmed its commitment to continue supporting fragile contexts such as the Democratic Republic of Congo, Somalia and South Sudan, while calling for increased mobilization by governments and international partners, noting that the lack of national financing and the decline in external aid are holding back the establishment of lasting programmes.

a6695.speaker: US Federal Reserve
a6695.name: US Federal Reserve
a6695.speech: Insisted for months that inflation is "transitory" ; hiked by 0.75pc and indicated it might do so again.

a6695.speaker: Most economists
a6695.name: Most economists
a6695.speech: Most economists now expect a recession - two consecutive quarters of negative growth.

a6695.speaker: A major edible oil producer in Kenya (unnamed)
a6695.name: A major edible oil producer in Kenya (unnamed)
a6695.speech: Cut production, citing a dollar shortage to import inputs.

a6695.speaker: Pakistani officials
a6695.name: Pakistani officials
a6695.speech: Called for a cut back on chai, a popular drink made from tea leaves (which are imported).

a6887.speaker: Judge Marelise du Plessis, Fishrot trial judge (court ruling)
a6887.name: Judge Marelise du Plessis
a6887.title: Fishrot trial judge (court ruling)
a6887.speech: Has rejected an application for her recusal in the ongoing Fishrot trial.

a6887.speaker: Sacky Shanghala, Fishrot accused and former Justice Minister (court application)
a6887.name: Sacky Shanghala
a6887.title: Fishrot accused and former Justice Minister (court application)
a6887.speech: Brought the recusal application, with James Hatuikulipi and Mike Nghipunya as co-applicants, asking the trial judge in the Fishrot corruption case to step aside ; has again filed an application in the High Court seeking to halt the Fishrot trial scheduled for August 4.

a6887.speaker: Sacky Shanghala, former Justice Minister
a6887.name: Sacky Shanghala
a6887.title: former Justice Minister
a6887.speech: Has bemoaned the continued separation of the Fishrot accused at the Windhoek Correctional Facility, arguing that it hampers their ability to prepare for trial.

a6887.speaker: Ministry of Justice and Labour Relations (Namibia)
a6887.name: Ministry of Justice and Labour Relations (Namibia)
a6887.speech: Says it does not wish to be drawn into commenting on the remuneration of individual public prosecutors amid allegations raised in the Windhoek High Court over pay disparities in the Fishrot corruption trial.

a6887.speaker: Audrin Mathe, Executive Director in the Ministry of Justice
a6887.name: Audrin Mathe
a6887.title: Executive Director in the Ministry of Justice
a6887.speech: Has said the ministry will issue a response on Monday following questions raised about the tariffs of the Legal Aid programme and alleged disparities in remuneration between defence lawyers and prosecutors in the Fishrot corruption trial.

a6887.speaker: Legal experts
a6887.name: Legal experts
a6887.speech: Are cautioning against the misuse of foundational legal doctrines in attempts to stall justice.

a6887.speaker: Martha Imalwa, Prosecutor General (Namibia)
a6887.name: Martha Imalwa
a6887.title: Prosecutor General (Namibia)
a6887.speech: Has dismissed claims that the Fishrot case is too complex for unrepresented accused, arguing that there is sufficient evidence to prove their guilt.

a6887.speaker: Justice Moses Chinhengo
a6887.name: Justice Moses Chinhengo
a6887.speech: Urged the accused, including former ministers Sakeus Shanghala and Bernhard Esau, to secure legal representation to ensure a fair trial.

a6990.speaker: Prof. Francis Bruno Zotor, Professor of Public Health Nutrition, Fred Newton Binka School of Public Health, University of Health and Allied Sciences, Ho
a6990.name: Prof. Francis Bruno Zotor
a6990.title: Professor of Public Health Nutrition, Fred Newton Binka School of Public Health, University of Health and Allied Sciences, Ho
a6990.speech: Has reiterated the need for Ghana to prioritise nutrition, particularly maternal nutrition, stressing that this is vital for protecting the lives of newborns and securing the country's future ; emphasised that fetal development is closely linked to maternal nutrition: “When the mother conceives or is pregnant, that mother has to eat the right nutrition. The kind of nutrition that the woman eats is very important, is very critical, because that baby would need the right nutrients to grow into a healthy, bouncing baby” ; “When you talk about maternal nutrition, if a woman does not eat healthily, that woman cannot give birth to a healthy, bouncing baby. That is why it's very critical for us to be concerned about the nutrition of the mother.”

a6990.speaker: Prof. Francis Bruno Zotor, Professor of Public Health Nutrition, University of Health and Allied Sciences, Ho
a6990.name: Prof. Francis Bruno Zotor
a6990.title: Professor of Public Health Nutrition, University of Health and Allied Sciences, Ho
a6990.speech: Expressed concern that despite Ghana's abundance of food, particularly the rich nutritional value of many indigenous dishes, these have largely been overlooked in favour of junk foods: “Ghana still has a long way to go because we see a situation where there is an abundance of food. Wherever you are in the country, there are certain indigenous foods that we can eat and that will provide the health that we need, rather than looking to the West and importing” ; called for increased public sensitisation on the nutritional benefits of indigenous foods: “We've got to begin to educate mothers, fathers, and teenagers—everybody in society—about eating foods that are available within their local community. That is the only way forward. But if we rely on foods that are imported, there is nothing in it; there is no benefit to us.”

a6990.speaker: Prof. Francis Bruno Zotor, Professor of Public Health Nutrition, University of Health and Allied Sciences, Ho
a6990.name: Prof. Francis Bruno Zotor
a6990.title: Professor of Public Health Nutrition, University of Health and Allied Sciences, Ho
a6990.speech: Stated that the withdrawal of funding by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), amounting to $163 million, has left several organisations struggling to sustain their projects; said this development is a wake-up call, highlighting the urgent need for Ghana to shift from donor dependence and explore local resources and solutions: “Ghana as a country can wake up from the doldrums and begin to look around. Use the academics, use the scientists, agriculturalists, nutritionists, the dieticians, the food scientists, let us come together at the round table. If we look up to the West, the West cannot help us. If we look up to other bodies, they cannot help us. But we can look at what we have within our environment and be able to help ourselves” ; said a collaborative national effort is needed to harness local knowledge and innovation for sustainable development.

a6990.speaker: Dr. Charity Binka, Executive Director of Women, Media and Change (WOMEC)
a6990.name: Dr. Charity Binka
a6990.title: Executive Director of Women, Media and Change (WOMEC)
a6990.speech: Emphasised that strengthening nutrition advocacy calls for strategic collaboration with the media to ensure the message reaches the wider population: “Step up advocacy around nutrition by working effectively with the media, because many people depend on the media for vital information. If the media is missing from this whole discussion, then who is talking to whom? The media platform is such a huge platform that one word from a radio station can go beyond the borders of Ghana” ; urged the media to take a more intentional approach to educating the public on malnutrition: “Apart from the funding we are looking for, education is so key to whatever we are saying here today. We can have all the policies, we can even get all the funding, if there's nobody to amplify the voices of the experts to let people know that this is what it is, that is why we are getting involved.”

a6990.speaker: Dr. Kasim Abdulai, Director of Operations, Coalition of Actors for Public Health Advocacy (CAPHA)
a6990.name: Dr. Kasim Abdulai
a6990.title: Director of Operations, Coalition of Actors for Public Health Advocacy (CAPHA)
a6990.speech: Said malnutrition costs Ghana GH₵4.6 billion annually in lost productivity and healthcare expenses ; noted that CAPHA, in collaboration with its partners, is conducting a study on maternal and child nutrition funding, focusing on the potential impact of USAID's withdrawal from Ghana, which will assess the existing funding landscape, identify key funding gaps, evaluate the potential consequences of USAID's withdrawal on the sustainability of programmes, and explore strategies to mitigate any negative impacts.

a7165.speaker: United States (announcement)
a7165.name: United States (announcement)
a7165.speech: Announced the suspension of foreign aid, which has sent shockwaves throughout Zambia, particularly for those relying on antiretroviral therapy (ARVs) to manage HIV/AIDS.

a7165.speaker: US Embassy in Zambia
a7165.name: US Embassy in Zambia
a7165.speech: Has assured that the suspension doesn't affect the entire program of support.

a7165.speaker: Dr. Kebby Musokotwane, Director General of the National AIDS Council
a7165.name: Dr. Kebby Musokotwane
a7165.title: Director General of the National AIDS Council
a7165.speech: Noted, “Mr. Trump’s orders were quite clear, but they don’t affect the whole programme of support.”

a7230.speaker: Committee of Concerned Scientists (letter dated April 8, 2025 to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Antonio Rubio)
a7230.name: Committee of Concerned Scientists (letter dated April 8
a7230.title: 2025 to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Antonio Rubio)
a7230.speech: Appealed to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Antonio Rubio, urging action; highlighted a $480 million Millennium Challenge Corporation agreement between the U.S. and Sierra Leone, signed under the previous administration, as leverage to press for improved human rights and accountability; called on the U.S. to secure Dr. Bah's right to return to Sierra Leone and continue his scholarly and journalistic work without fear while demanding an investigation into the threats against him.

a7424.speaker: Jim Risch, senior US lawmaker (US Senator)
a7424.name: Jim Risch
a7424.title: senior US lawmaker (US Senator)
a7424.speech: Criticised Ghana’s government over debts owed to American companies and taxpayers.

a7424.speaker: US Senate Foreign Relations Committee (social media post)
a7424.name: US Senate Foreign Relations Committee (social media post)
a7424.speech: Suggested that Ghana’s Foreign Minister should stay home and prioritise paying outstanding debts rather than travelling to Washington for diplomatic engagements; accused Ghana of continuing to pay larger debts to China while allegedly defaulting on its financial obligations to American entities: “Instead of a trip to D.C., Ghana’s foreign minister should focus on honoring his government’s commitments to repay U.S. companies and the American taxpayers. We cannot keep subsidizing Ghana while it continues paying far larger debts to China.”

a7424.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Ghana’s Minister for Foreign Affairs
a7424.name: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa
a7424.title: Ghana’s Minister for Foreign Affairs
a7424.speech: Rejected the comments and described the remarks as “very rich” coming from a country that has consistently failed to confront and atone for its involvement in the slave trade: “This is very rich coming from someone who refuses to engage in the same advocacy for the payment of reparations by the US for its despicable and condemnable role in slavery.”

a7424.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Ghana’s Minister for Foreign Affairs
a7424.name: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa
a7424.title: Ghana’s Minister for Foreign Affairs
a7424.speech: Declared, referencing Ghana’s founding father Dr Kwame Nkrumah: “You will not be allowed to dictate to a sovereign country on how we conduct our foreign policy — if you need to be reminded — this is Kwame Nkrumah’s Ghana — the first African nation to defeat colonialism and imperialism.”

a7424.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Ghana’s Minister for Foreign Affairs
a7424.name: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa
a7424.title: Ghana’s Minister for Foreign Affairs
a7424.speech: Stated, while acknowledging that Ghana owes debts to some American companies: “Those measly debts, compared to what you owe us in reparations, would be paid when we deem appropriate based on our prudent economic recovery program — even though the debt was not created by the new Mahama administration” ; concluded by stressing Ghana’s commitment to fulfilling its obligations: “Unlike you, we take responsibility and honour our national obligations.”
